definition_zh: 领空；空域；可供飞行的开阔天空
definition_en: the sky above a country, regarded as its territory, or a defined area of sky used for a particular purpose
core_image: 国界线笔直向上延伸，裹住一柱有归属的天空
scene: 机场塔台里，值班员盯着雷达上不断移动的光点。The pilot waited for clearance to enter the country's airspace.
sceneCN: 这里 airspace 是「领空」（第 1 个义项：一国管辖的上方空域）；句意为飞行员等待进入该国领空的许可。

pos.zh: 名词：领空；空域；可供飞行的天空

derivatives.zh: 复合词首成分，义为「空气、天空」，源自希腊语 aēr
复合词第二成分，义为「空间」，源自拉丁语 spatium
与 airspace 共用 air 与 space 两个成分，义为「航空航天」

senses.title: The sky above a nation
senses.definition: the column of sky above a country, treated in law as part of its territory
senses.definitionCN: 一国领土上方的空域，在法律上被视为该国领土的一部分
senses.example: The aircraft was ordered to leave national airspace immediately.
senses.exampleCN: 这架飞机被要求立即离开该国领空。
senses.why: Air plus space turns the sky into a place: a border drawn on land can be extended straight upward, and the column it encloses belongs to someone.
senses.whyCN: air 与 space 合起来把天空变成一个地方：地上的国界可以笔直向上延伸，围出的这一柱空气就有了归属。

senses.title: A controlled zone of sky
senses.definition: a defined block of sky that an authority sets aside for a purpose or controls for safety
senses.definitionCN: 由主管机构划定用途或为安全而加以管制的特定天空区块
senses.example: Controllers divided the airspace into arrival and departure corridors.
senses.exampleCN: 管制员把这片空域划分为进港和离港走廊。
senses.why: Once the sky is a place, it can be surveyed and cut into blocks, just as land is cut into districts with rules for each.
senses.whyCN: 天空一旦成为地方，就能像土地划区那样被测量、切块，并为每一块定下规则。

senses.title: Open sky available for flight
senses.definition: the open sky left free for aircraft, kites, or other flying objects
senses.definitionCN: 留供飞机、风筝或其他飞行物使用的开阔天空
senses.example: The kite climbed until it reached open airspace above the trees.
senses.exampleCN: 风筝一直上升，直到进入树梢之上的开阔空域。
senses.why: This is the compound at its plainest: air as empty room and space as room to move, with no border or controller in sight.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个复合词最朴素的用法：air 是空气，space 是可活动的余地，既没有边界也没有管制员。

intro.en: Airspace joins a Greek word for the misty lower air to a Latin word for extent, and aviation gave the pair a legal meaning.
intro.cn: airspace 把希腊语中表示低处雾气般空气的词，接到拉丁语表示范围、空间的词上，航空业又给这对组合添了法律含义。

items.en: Greek aēr named the lower, misty air that people breathe, as opposed to the bright upper sky.
items.cn: 希腊语 aēr 指人呼吸的、低处带雾的空气，与明亮的上层天空相对。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as aer, still meaning air, and passed it to French and English.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊词作 aer，仍指空气，再经法语传入英语。

items.en: Old French air carried the word into English, where air soon also meant the open sky.
items.cn: 古法语 air 把这个词带入英语，air 很快也指开阔的天空。

items.en: Latin spatium meant an extent or interval, the source of English space and of spacious.
items.cn: 拉丁语 spatium 意为范围、间隔，是英语 space 与 spacious 的来源。

items.en: Aviation needed one word for the sky as property and as a managed zone, so air and space were joined.
items.cn: 航空业需要用一个词同时表达「作为财产的天空」和「被管理的天空」，于是把 air 与 space 合在一起。

items.en: Treaties fixed the principle that each state controls the airspace above its land and waters.
items.cn: 各项条约确立了每个国家管辖其陆地与水域上方领空的原则。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built from the same two halves; the near-meaning group gathers words for sky, territory and zones.
note.cn: 形近组收由同样两个成分构成的词；近义组收表示天空、领土与区域的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the mixture of gases around the earth, also used for the open sky.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指地球周围的气体混合物，也用来指开阔的天空。

entries.definition: The noun for room or extent, the second half of airspace.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指空间或范围，是 airspace 的后半部分。

entries.definition: The industry and technology of aircraft and spacecraft together.
entries.definitionCN: 指航空与航天合在一起的产业与技术。

entries.definition: The visible space above the earth, without any legal or managed sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指地面上方可见的空间，不带法律或管制含义。

entries.definition: An area under a state's control, usually land, but law can extend it upward.
entries.definitionCN: 指一国控制的区域，通常是陆地，法律也可将其向上延伸。

entries.definition: An area marked off for a particular purpose, the model behind a controlled airspace block.
entries.definitionCN: 指为特定用途划出的区域，是管制空域区块的模型。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the compound into air and space and attach each half to something you can see.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把复合词拆成 air 与 space，并让每一半都挂上看得见的东西。

normal.en: Airspace is air plus space: the sky treated as real estate.
normal.cn: airspace 是 air 加 space：把天空当成地产。

normal.en: A border on the ground can be drawn upward, and the column above it is national airspace.
normal.cn: 地上的国界可以向上画，它上方的那一柱就是领空。

normal.en: Controlled airspace is sky with lanes and rules, like a highway in the air.
normal.cn: controlled airspace 是有航线和规则的天空，像空中的高速公路。

normal.en: A drone that crosses a line without permission violates airspace.
normal.cn: 无人机未经许可越过界线，就是侵犯领空。

normal.en: Open airspace is simply room to fly, with no owner and no controller.
normal.cn: open airspace 只是可供飞行的余地，没有归属也没有管制。

abstract.en: Picture a fence standing on a hill, then pull the fence straight up into the clouds.
abstract.cn: 想象山顶上立着一道篱笆，再把这道篱笆笔直拉进云里。

abstract.en: The fence leaves a shadow-column of sky behind it, and that column has a name.
abstract.cn: 篱笆在身后留下一柱带影子的天空，这一柱天空有了名字。

abstract.en: Turn the column sideways and it becomes a corridor through which planes slide.
abstract.cn: 把这一柱天空横过来，它就成了飞机穿行的走廊。

examples.en: The drone flew into restricted airspace near the border.
examples.cn: 无人机飞入了边境附近的限制空域。

examples.en: The tower closed the airspace because of heavy fog.
examples.cn: 塔台因大雾关闭了该空域。

examples.en: Every country claims the airspace above its territory.
examples.cn: 每个国家都主张其领土上方的领空。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「空气 空间」——空气加空间，就是划出来的一片天

root: 英语复合词：air（空气、天空，源自希腊语 aēr，经拉丁语 aer 与古法语 air 入英语）+ space（空间，源自拉丁语 spatium），字面为「天空中的一片空间」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses treat the sky as national territory, as a managed zone, and as open room for flight.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项分别把天空看作国家领土、被管理的区域，以及可供飞行的开阔空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a border line on the ground is extended straight upward, and the column of sky above it becomes a place with an owner.
core.cn: 核心意象：地上的国界线笔直向上延伸，它上方那一柱天空就成了有归属的地方。

branches.en: THE BORDER: the line on the ground rises into the sky and marks an owned column of air.
branches.cn: 边界线：地上的线升到空中，标出一柱有归属的空气。

branches.en: THE STATE: international law accepts that a country's territory includes the sky above it.
branches.cn: 国家线：国际法承认一国领土包括其上方天空。

branches.en: THE MANAGER: aviation authorities cut the sky into blocks with rules and corridors.
branches.cn: 管理线：航空当局用规则和走廊把天空切成块。

branches.en: THE OPEN SKY: beyond the controlled blocks there is still room for a kite or a glider.
branches.cn: 开阔线：在管制区块之外，仍有供风筝或滑翔机使用的空间。

branches.en: THE CROSSING: a flight moves from one controlled block into open sky and back again.
branches.cn: 穿越线：一次飞行从某个管制区块进入开阔天空，再返回。

intro.en: Airspace is a transparent English compound whose interest lies in joining a natural element to a legal idea of space.
intro.cn: airspace 是一个透明的英语复合词，其趣味在于把自然元素接到法律意义上的空间概念上。

latinIntro.en: Both halves reach back through Latin to Greek or to an older Latin stem, and the deeper origin of each is only partly certain.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都经由拉丁语上溯到希腊语或更早的拉丁词干，各自更深的来源只部分确定。

items.meaning: the mixture of gases we breathe

items.example: The box takes up little space.
items.exampleCN: 这个盒子占的空间很小。
它构成 airmail 与 airspace。
管制员重新划分了这个空域块。

items.meaning: an aircraft operator using the sky
items.example: Every airspace user must file a flight plan.
items.exampleCN: 每个空域使用者都必须提交飞行计划。

definition_zh: 警报；警报器；惊恐；闹钟；使惊恐；警示
definition_en: a warning sound or device, the fear it causes, or to make someone feel sudden fear
core_image: 半夜突然响起的铃，把熟睡的人一把拽下床
scene: 深夜厨房飘出焦味，墙上的小盒子忽然尖声叫起来。The smoke alarm woke the whole family at three in the morning.
sceneCN: 这里 alarm 是「警报器」（第 1 个义项：发出警报的装置）；句意为烟雾警报器在凌晨三点叫醒了全家。

pos.zh: 名词：警报；警报器；惊恐；闹钟
动词：使惊恐；使担忧；向……报警

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「令人惊恐的；令人担忧的」
由 alarming 加 -ly 构成，义为「惊人地；令人担忧地」
由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「危言耸听者」
由动词过去分词转化而来，义为「惊恐的；担忧的」

senses.title: A warning device or sound
senses.definition: a device or loud sound that warns people of danger, fire, or an intruder
senses.definitionCN: 用来警告人们有危险、火情或入侵者的装置或响亮声音
senses.example: The fire alarm rang through the whole building.
senses.exampleCN: 火警警报响彻整栋大楼。
senses.why: The word began as a shout telling soldiers to take up arms; the shout became a machine that still gives the same order.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是叫士兵拿起武器的呼喊；呼喊后来变成一台机器，仍在下达同一道命令。

senses.title: Sudden fear
senses.definition: the fear and anxiety people feel when they sense danger
senses.definitionCN: 人们察觉危险时感到的恐惧与焦虑
senses.example: She looked at the broken window in alarm.
senses.exampleCN: 她惊恐地看着那扇破窗。
senses.why: The cry to arms also named the feeling it produced: the shout and the shudder were stored in one word.
senses.whyCN: 拿起武器的呼喊也命名了它引发的感受：喊声与战栗被存进了同一个词里。

senses.title: A clock that rings
senses.definition: a clock that makes a loud sound at a set time to wake someone
senses.definitionCN: 在设定时间发出响亮声音以叫醒人的钟
senses.example: He set the alarm for half past five.
senses.exampleCN: 他把闹钟定在五点半。
senses.why: A clock alarm does what a battlefield alarm did: it interrupts sleep with a command to act now.
senses.whyCN: 闹钟做的事和战场警报一样：用一道立刻行动的命令打断睡眠。

senses.title: To frighten or warn
senses.definition: to make someone feel worried or frightened, or to warn them of danger
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到担忧或恐惧，或向其警示危险
senses.example: The rising cost of fuel alarmed the farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料成本上涨让农民们感到担忧。
senses.why: The verb applies the shout directly to a person: the warning cry enters the listener and becomes fear.
senses.whyCN: 动词把喊声直接作用在人身上：警告的呼喊进入听者，变成恐惧。

intro.en: Alarm is a battlefield shout that became a machine, a feeling, and a clock.
intro.cn: alarm 是一声战场呼喝，后来变成机器、感受和闹钟。

items.en: Italian all'arme meant 'to arms!', the shout that called soldiers to battle.
items.cn: 意大利语 all'arme 意为「拿起武器！」，是召士兵出战的呼喊。

items.en: Old French alarme borrowed the shout as a noun for a call to arms and the fear it spread.
items.cn: 古法语 alarme 借入这声呼喊，作名词指召集出战的号令及由此散开的恐惧。

items.en: English alarm first named a sudden call to arms, then any warning of danger.
items.cn: 英语 alarm 先指突然的出战号令，后指任何危险警告。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the noun also meant the panic itself, not only the signal.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个名词也指惊慌本身，而不只是信号。

items.en: The clock alarm borrowed the same idea: a signal that forces a sleeper to act.
items.cn: 闹钟借用了同一观念：一个迫使睡眠者行动的信号。

items.en: The verb appeared later and turned the signal into an action done to a person.
items.cn: 动词出现得更晚，把信号变成施加在人身上的一种动作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the alarm family; the near-meaning group gathers warnings, signals and kinds of fear.
note.cn: 形近组收 alarm 词族；近义组收警告、信号与各类恐惧。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning causing worry or fear.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人担忧的、令人惊恐的」。

entries.definition: A person who spreads unnecessary warnings of danger.
entries.definitionCN: 指散布不必要的危险警告的人。

entries.definition: A clock that rings at a chosen time.
entries.definitionCN: 指在设定时间响铃的钟。

entries.definition: A statement or sign that danger is coming, often given in words.
entries.definitionCN: 指危险将至的言语或迹象，多以话语给出。

entries.definition: A state of readiness or a signal that puts people on guard.
entries.definitionCN: 指戒备状态，或使人警惕起来的信号。

entries.definition: A loud wailing device used on police cars or in air raids.
entries.definitionCN: 指警车或空袭中使用的尖厉鸣响装置。

entries.definition: Sudden uncontrollable fear that spreads through a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指在人群中蔓延的、突然无法控制的恐惧。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the shout from the battlefield to the bedroom wall.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子沿着这声呼喊，从战场一路跟到卧室墙边。

normal.en: Alarm began as a cry to arms, so its loudness is the point.
normal.cn: alarm 原本是拿起武器的呼喊，所以「响」才是它的要害。

normal.en: The same word is the shout, the fear, and the clock that repeats the shout.
normal.cn: 同一个词既是喊声，也是恐惧，还是重复喊声的钟。

normal.en: Raise the alarm is to start the warning; in alarm is to be inside the fear.
normal.cn: raise the alarm 是发出警告；in alarm 是置身恐惧之中。

normal.en: Alarm bells ringing in your head means something feels wrong before proof arrives.
normal.cn: 脑中的 alarm bells 响起，意味着证据未到就先觉得不对。

normal.en: An alarm clock is a tiny battlefield on the bedside table.
normal.cn: 闹钟是床头柜上的一小片战场。

abstract.en: Picture a sentry's shout crossing a dark field and reaching a row of sleeping soldiers.
abstract.cn: 想象哨兵的一声喊穿过黑暗的原野，传到一排熟睡的士兵耳中。

abstract.en: The shout does not need words: a bell, a siren and a phone can all carry it.
abstract.cn: 这声喊不需要词语：铃、汽笛和电话都能承载它。

abstract.en: Shrink the shout into a small box on the wall, and it becomes the alarm we know.
abstract.cn: 把喊声缩进墙上的小盒子，它就成了我们熟悉的警报器。

examples.en: The burglar alarm went off just as the door opened.
examples.cn: 门刚一打开，防盗警报就响了。

examples.en: There is no cause for alarm; the test results are normal.
examples.cn: 不必惊慌，检查结果正常。

examples.en: She set her alarm early so she could catch the first bus.
examples.cn: 她把闹钟定得很早，好赶上头班车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，拉姆」——啊的一声拉响警报，拉姆冲下楼

root: 源自意大利语 all'arme「拿起武器」，经古法语 alarme 进入英语；原为战场上的紧急呼喝，后指警报、警报器与随之而来的惊恐。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses follow one shout as it becomes a warning device, a feeling of fear, a waking clock, and finally a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项跟着同一声呼喊，看它变成警告装置、恐惧感受、叫醒人的钟，最后变成动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentry's shout cuts across a dark field, and everyone who hears it jumps up at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：哨兵的一声喊划过黑暗的原野，听到的人全都一跃而起。

branches.en: THE SHOUT: the original cry to arms is still audible in the device that now gives it.
branches.cn: 喊声线：最初的出战呼喊，仍能在如今发出它的装置里听见。

branches.en: THE SHUDDER: the same cry names the fear that runs through the people who hear it.
branches.cn: 战栗线：同一喊声也命名了听者身上蔓延的恐惧。

branches.en: THE BEDSIDE: a clock repeats the cry every morning at a chosen hour.
branches.cn: 床头线：闹钟每天早上在选定时刻重复这声喊。

branches.en: THE VERB: the cry is aimed at a person, and the warning becomes an act.
branches.cn: 动词线：喊声对准某个人，警告就变成一种行为。

branches.en: THE RING: a bell can carry both the signal and the fear without a single word.
branches.cn: 铃声线：一只铃不用一个词，就能同时承载信号与恐惧。

intro.en: Alarm is a borrowed shout with a small English family built on it; the suffixes are ordinary, the history is not.
intro.cn: alarm 是一声借来的呼喊，上面长出一个不大的英语词族；后缀平常，历史却不平常。

latinIntro.en: The word entered English through Italian and French, not through Latin, so its Latin entries are indirect.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经意大利语和法语进入英语，而非直接来自拉丁语，所以它的拉丁条目是间接的。

items.example: The phrase was a battlefield order.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语曾是战场命令。

items.meaning: a person who does or believes
items.meaningCN: 从事某事或信奉某事的人

items.example: My alarm clock is too loud.
The fire alarm emptied the hall.
items.exampleCN: 火警警报让大厅里的人全撤了出去。

items.meaning: a bell used as a warning

definition_zh: 相册；音乐专辑；集邮册；纪念册
definition_en: a book with blank pages for photographs or stamps, or a set of recorded songs released together
core_image: 一本贴满照片的厚册子，翻一页就是一段时光
scene: 祖母把散落的旧照片一张张贴进那本厚册子。She pasted the old photographs into a leather album.
sceneCN: 这里 album 是「相册」（第 1 个义项：贴放照片的册子）；句意为她把旧照片贴进一本皮面相册。

pos.zh: 名词：相册；音乐专辑；集邮册；纪念册

derivatives.zh: 复合名词，义为「专辑封面」，由 album 与 cover 组合而成
复合名词，义为「专辑曲目」，指专辑中的一首歌
复合名词，义为「相册」，由 photo 与 album 组合而成

senses.title: A book for photographs
senses.definition: a book with blank or pocketed pages in which photographs are kept
senses.definitionCN: 用来存放照片的册子，页面空白或带有插袋
senses.example: They spent the evening looking through their wedding album.
senses.exampleCN: 他们花了一晚上翻看婚礼相册。
senses.why: Latin albus meant white, and an album was first a white surface to write on; a photo album is still a set of white pages waiting to be filled.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 albus 意为白色，album 最初指可书写的白色表面；相册仍是一叠等待被填满的白页。

senses.title: A collection of recorded songs
senses.definition: a set of songs or pieces released together as one unit, on disc or in digital form
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个单元一起发行的一组歌曲或乐曲，刻在唱片上或以数字形式发行
senses.example: The band's new album sold out in a single day.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队的新专辑一天就卖光了。
senses.why: The blank-page book became a container for collected works, and recorded songs inherited the same idea of a gathered set.
senses.whyCN: 空白页册子变成收集作品的容器，录制的歌曲继承了同一个「聚成一集」的观念。

senses.title: A book for stamps or autographs
senses.definition: a book kept for collecting stamps, signatures, or other small flat items
senses.definitionCN: 用来收集邮票、签名或其他小型扁平物品的册子
senses.example: His grandfather kept every stamp in a worn album.
senses.exampleCN: 他祖父把每一枚邮票都收在一本磨损的集邮册里。
senses.why: This is the original book sense at its most literal: pages exist only to hold what someone chooses to collect.
senses.whyCN: 这是「册子」本义最字面的用法：页面的存在只为盛放某人选择收集的东西。

intro.en: Album starts at a white writing surface and ends as a container for photographs and songs.
intro.cn: album 从一种白色的书写表面出发，最后成了照片与歌曲的容器。

items.en: Latin albus meant white, and it also gave albumen and albumin, words for the white of an egg.
items.cn: 拉丁语 albus 意为白色，还生出 albumen 与 albumin，指蛋清。

items.en: An album was a blank white tablet or board on which public notices and lists of names were written.
items.cn: album 原指空白的白色板子或书写板，用来写公告和名单。

items.en: English borrowed album for a blank book in which people collected notes, drawings, or signatures.
items.cn: 英语借入 album，指供人收集笔记、图画或签名的空白册子。

items.en: Photography gave the book its modern job: page after page of mounted photographs.
items.cn: 摄影给它添了现代职务：一页接一页贴放照片。

items.en: The record industry reused the word for a set of songs sold together, first as a book of discs.
items.cn: 唱片业把这个词再次用于成套出售的歌曲，最初指装有唱片的小册。

items.en: The container no longer needs paper, but the word still means a gathered set.
items.cn: 容器不再需要纸张，但这个词仍表示聚在一起的一整套作品。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the white root; the near-meaning group gathers books and sets that hold collected things.
note.cn: 形近组收来自「白色」词根的词；近义组收盛放收集之物的册子与成套作品。

entries.definition: The white of an egg, named from the Latin word for white.
entries.definitionCN: 指蛋清，得名于拉丁语中表示白色的词。

entries.definition: A family of proteins, including the white part of egg.
entries.definitionCN: 指一类蛋白质，包括蛋清中的蛋白。

entries.definition: The printed outer cover of a music album.
entries.definitionCN: 指音乐专辑印制的封面。

entries.definition: A book in which cuttings, pictures and notes are pasted.
entries.definitionCN: 指粘贴剪报、图片和笔记的册子。

entries.definition: A disc or collection of recorded music, an older word for an album.
entries.definitionCN: 指唱片或成套录制的音乐，是 album 的旧称。

entries.definition: A group of things gathered together, often by one person.
entries.definitionCN: 指聚在一起的一组物品，常由一人收集。

entries.definition: A flat case or book holding drawings, photographs or documents.
entries.definitionCN: 指存放图画、照片或文件的扁平盒子或册子。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the white page in view while the contents change from stamps to songs.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子始终盯住那页白纸，只是内容从邮票换成了歌曲。

normal.en: Album first meant a white board for names, so think white page before thinking songs.
normal.cn: album 最初指写名字的白板，所以先想白页，再想歌曲。

normal.en: A photo album is a book whose only job is to hold pictures.
normal.cn: photo album 是一本唯一职务就是装照片的册子。

normal.en: A music album is the same container idea moved into sound.
normal.cn: 音乐专辑是把同一个容器观念搬进声音里。

normal.en: Debut album is the first set a band releases, the opening page of a career.
normal.cn: debut album 是乐队发行的第一套作品，是职业生涯的首页。

normal.en: Album cover is the page turned into a poster.
normal.cn: album cover 是把册页变成海报。

abstract.en: Picture a white tablet on a wall, covered with names written in ink.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的一块白色板子，写满了墨水的名字。

abstract.en: Fold the tablet into pages and the names become photographs.
abstract.cn: 把板子折成书页，名字就变成了照片。

abstract.en: Play the pages as sound and the album becomes a record.
abstract.cn: 把书页当作声音播放，album 就成了唱片。

examples.en: She keeps every family photo in a thick album.
examples.cn: 她把每张家庭照片都收在一本厚相册里。

examples.en: The singer released her first album at nineteen.
examples.cn: 这位歌手十九岁时发行了首张专辑。

examples.en: He opened the album and found a stamp from 1950.
examples.cn: 他翻开集邮册，找到一枚一九五零年的邮票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱儿本」——爱儿本里贴满孩子从小到大的照片

root: 拉丁语 albus「白色」→ album「白色书写板、名单」→ 空白页册子 → 相册、集邮册，再到成套发行的音乐专辑。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses are one container seen with different contents: photographs, recorded songs, and collected small items.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项是同一个容器装上不同内容：照片、录制的歌曲，以及收集来的小物件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick book of blank white pages lies open, and every page waits to hold one kept thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本厚厚的白页册子摊开着，每一页都在等待盛放一件被珍藏的东西。

branches.en: THE BLANK PAGE: the oldest sense is simply a white surface reserved for written names.
branches.cn: 白页线：最古老的义项只是留供书写名字的白色表面。

branches.en: THE PHOTO: the blank page takes on its most familiar job, holding pictures.
branches.cn: 照片线：白页承担最熟悉的职务，盛放图片。

branches.en: THE STAMP: small flat treasures also need pages, so the same book serves collectors.
branches.cn: 邮票线：小型扁平珍藏也需要页面，同一册子于是服务于收藏者。

branches.en: THE SONG: the container moves from paper to sound and holds a set of recordings.
branches.cn: 歌曲线：容器从纸转到声音，盛放一整套录音。

branches.en: THE SET: whether pictures or songs, the word insists that things are gathered and kept together.
branches.cn: 成套线：无论图片还是歌曲，这个词都强调东西被聚拢并保存。

intro.en: Album is a Latin loanword with almost no derivational family; its compounds carry the modern meanings.
intro.cn: album 是拉丁语借词，几乎没有派生词族；现代含义主要由复合词承担。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base albus is well recorded; its deeper Indo-European origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 albus 有明确记录，它更早的印欧来源不确定。

items.example: The Latin word meant a blank board.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词指空白板子。

items.example: It is the source of album and albumen.
items.exampleCN: 它是 album 与 albumen 的来源。

items.example: It marks the Latin form album.
items.exampleCN: 它标出拉丁语形式 album。

items.example: She showed us her photo album.

items.meaning: the outer cover of an album
items.example: The album cover won a design prize.
items.exampleCN: 这张专辑封面得了设计奖。

items.meaning: a set of recordings in one package
items.example: He owns an original record album.

definition_zh: 酒精；乙醇；酒；饮酒
definition_en: the clear liquid in beer and wine that makes people drunk, or drinks containing it
core_image: 一只细颈瓶里清澈的液体，闻起来辛辣，靠近火就能点燃
scene: 诊所里，护士拧开一瓶透明液体，蘸了棉球擦洗伤口。The nurse cleaned the cut with alcohol before bandaging it.
sceneCN: 这里 alcohol 是「酒精」（第 1 个义项：用于消毒的乙醇）；句意为护士上药前用酒精清洗伤口。

pos.zh: 名词：酒精；乙醇；酒；饮酒行为

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「含酒精的」；亦可作名词指酗酒者
由本词加 -ism 构成，义为「酒精成瘾；酗酒」
由本词加 -free 构成，义为「不含酒精的」

senses.title: Ethanol as a chemical
senses.definition: the colourless liquid ethanol, used as a solvent, fuel, or disinfectant
senses.definitionCN: 无色液体乙醇，用作溶剂、燃料或消毒剂
senses.example: The laboratory stores alcohol in a locked cabinet.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把酒精锁在柜子里。
senses.why: The word first named a fine powder made by sublimation; chemistry then applied it to the refined spirit that evaporates and burns.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指升华制成的细粉；化学后来用它指那种会挥发、会燃烧的精炼液体。

senses.title: Drinks that contain it
senses.definition: beer, wine, and other drinks that contain ethanol
senses.definitionCN: 啤酒、葡萄酒及其他含乙醇的饮品
senses.example: The clinic offers advice to people who want to cut down on alcohol.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所向想减少饮酒的人提供建议。
senses.why: Because the liquid is what makes a drink intoxicating, the name of the substance was transferred to the drinks themselves.
senses.whyCN: 正因为这种液体使饮品醉人，物质的名字就被转用到饮品本身上。

senses.title: The habit of drinking
senses.definition: the practice or amount of drinking alcoholic beverages, especially when discussed as a social or health issue
senses.definitionCN: 饮用含酒精饮料的行为或数量，尤在作为社会或健康议题讨论时
senses.example: The report links easy access to alcohol with rising road accidents.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把酒精容易获得与道路事故上升联系起来。
senses.why: This sense names not the liquid but the human activity around it, the way a substance becomes a habit.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项指的不是液体，而是围绕它的人类活动，是物质变成习惯的过程。

intro.en: Alcohol travelled from an Arabic word for powdered antimony to the spirit of wine and then to drinks in general.
intro.cn: alcohol 从阿拉伯语中表示锑粉的词，走到酒之精华，再走到泛指酒类。

items.en: Arabic al-kuḥl named a fine powder of antimony used to darken the eyes, with al- as the definite article.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-kuḥl 指一种用来描黑眼睛的细锑粉，其中 al- 是定冠词。

items.en: Medieval Latin borrowed the word as alcohol, a powder obtained by sublimation, and the idea of refinement stuck.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语借入作 alcohol，指升华所得的细粉，「提炼」的观念由此留下。

items.en: English alcohol first meant a fine powder or distilled essence, not a drink.
items.cn: 英语 alcohol 最初指细粉或蒸馏所得的精粹，并不是饮品。

items.en: Chemists spoke of alcohol of wine for the volatile spirit released by distillation.
items.cn: 化学家说 alcohol of wine，指蒸馏释放出的挥发性精华。

items.en: Modern chemistry fixed alcohol as the class of compounds including ethanol.
items.cn: 现代化学把 alcohol 固定为包含乙醇的一类化合物。

items.en: Everyday English shortened alcohol of wine to alcohol and used it for intoxicating drinks.
items.cn: 日常英语把 alcohol of wine 缩为 alcohol，并用它指醉人的饮品。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the alcohol family; the near-meaning group gathers chemical and everyday names for the same or similar liquids.
note.cn: 形近组收 alcohol 词族；近义组收同一类或相近液体的化学名称与日常名称。

entries.definition: Containing alcohol, or a person dependent on drinking.
entries.definitionCN: 指含酒精的，或指依赖饮酒的人。

entries.definition: The medical condition of being unable to control drinking.
entries.definitionCN: 指无法控制饮酒的医学状况。

entries.definition: Describing a drink with no alcohol in it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容饮品不含酒精。

entries.definition: The chemical name for the alcohol in drinks and fuel.
entries.definitionCN: 指饮品和燃料中那种酒精的化学名称。

entries.definition: Strong distilled drink such as whisky or gin.
entries.definitionCN: 指威士忌、金酒等烈性蒸馏酒。

entries.definition: A strong distilled drink, from the older phrase spirit of wine.
entries.definitionCN: 指烈性蒸馏酒，来自旧说法「酒之精华」。

entries.definition: A drink made by fermenting grapes or other fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 指由葡萄或其他水果发酵制成的饮品。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the liquid from a powder in an Arab pharmacy to a bottle on a table.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子跟着这种液体，从阿拉伯药房里的粉末走到餐桌上的瓶子。

normal.en: Alcohol first meant a fine powder, so remember refinement before remembering drinking.
normal.cn: alcohol 最初指细粉，所以先记「提炼」，再记「饮酒」。

normal.en: The spirit of wine is the part that evaporates and burns; alcohol is that spirit named.
normal.cn: 酒之精华是会挥发、会燃烧的那部分；alcohol 就是被命名的这股精华。

normal.en: Alcohol content tells you how much of the substance a drink holds.
normal.cn: alcohol content 告诉你一杯饮品里含有多少这种物质。

normal.en: Rubbing alcohol is the same word in a clinic, doing a cleaning job instead of a social one.
normal.cn: rubbing alcohol 是同一个词进了诊所，干的是清洁而不是社交的活。

normal.en: Alcohol-free keeps the word but removes the thing, which is why the phrase is useful.
normal.cn: alcohol-free 保留词却去掉物，这正是这个说法有用的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a glass flask over a small flame, and a clear drop forming at the end of a tube.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃瓶架在小火上，一滴清澈液体在管口凝成。

abstract.en: The drop is the refined essence, the part the old chemists called the alcohol.
abstract.cn: 这滴液体就是提炼出的精华，旧时化学家称之为 alcohol。

abstract.en: Pour the drop into a glass and the same word becomes a drink.
abstract.cn: 把这滴液体倒进杯子，同一个词就变成了酒。

examples.en: This drink contains no alcohol, so children may have it.
examples.cn: 这种饮料不含酒精，孩子也可以喝。

examples.en: Doctors warn that alcohol increases the risk of liver disease.
examples.cn: 医生警告说酒精会增加肝病风险。

examples.en: He stopped drinking alcohol after the accident.
examples.cn: 那次事故后他戒了酒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱儿可好」——爱儿可好，别碰酒精

root: 源自阿拉伯语 al-kuḥl（锑粉，al- 为定冠词），经中世纪拉丁语 alcohol（升华所得的细粉）进入英语；词义由「提炼的精华」转为「蒸馏所得酒精」，再泛指酒类。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses move from the chemical substance to the drinks made with it, and then to the human habit around those drinks.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从化学物质，走到用它制成的饮品，再到围绕这些饮品的人类习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear drop condenses at the end of a still, and the drop can both burn and intoxicate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴清澈液体在蒸馏器口凝成，这滴液体既能燃烧，也能醉人。

branches.en: THE POWDER: the oldest sense was a refined powder, and refinement is the thread that survives.
branches.cn: 粉末线：最古老的义项是提炼出的细粉，「提炼」是存活下来的线索。

branches.en: THE STILL: distillation turns the powder idea into a volatile, flammable liquid.
branches.cn: 蒸馏线：蒸馏把粉末观念变成会挥发、可燃的液体。

branches.en: THE CHEMIST: chemistry fixes the word as a class of compounds, with ethanol as the familiar member.
branches.cn: 化学线：化学把这个词固定为一类化合物，乙醇是最熟悉的成员。

branches.en: THE GLASS: the substance gives its name to the drinks that carry it.
branches.cn: 酒杯线：物质把自己的名字给了承载它的饮品。

branches.en: THE HABIT: the word finally names what people do with the liquid, not the liquid itself.
branches.cn: 习惯线：这个词最终命名人们拿这种液体做的事，而不是液体本身。

intro.en: Alcohol is an Arabic loanword, so its affix work is mostly suffixes added in English and compounds naming uses.
intro.cn: alcohol 是阿拉伯语借词，所以它的构词工作多是由英语加上的后缀，以及命名用途的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The route runs through medieval Latin, but the base itself is Arabic, so there are no native Latin family entries.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经由中世纪拉丁语转手，但词基本身来自阿拉伯语，因此没有本土拉丁同族条目。

items.example: It begins the Arabic source word.
items.exampleCN: 它是阿拉伯语源词的开头。

items.example: The powder was used around the eyes.
Ethyl alcohol is used as fuel.

items.meaningCN: 用于清洁皮肤的外用酒精
items.example: She wiped the table with rubbing alcohol.

items.exampleCN: 这家诊所治疗酗酒问题。

definition_zh: 含酒精的；酒精引起的；酗酒者；酒精成瘾者
definition_en: containing alcohol, caused by alcohol, or a person who cannot control their drinking
core_image: 一个人扶着桌沿，杯子还握在手里，眼神已经飘远
scene: 聚会散场后，他仍坐在角落，一杯接一杯。Her father was an alcoholic who could not stop drinking.
sceneCN: 这里 alcoholic 是「酗酒者」（第 2 个义项：酒精成瘾的人）；句意为她父亲是个停不下来的酗酒者。

pos.zh: 形容词：含酒精的；由酒精引起的
名词：酗酒者；酒精成瘾者

derivatives.zh: 去掉形容词后缀得到的基础名词，义为「酒精」
由 alcohol 加 -ism 构成，义为「酒精成瘾」
由否定前缀 non- 加本词构成，义为「不含酒精的」

senses.title: Containing alcohol
senses.definition: describing a drink that contains ethanol
senses.definitionCN: 形容含有乙醇的饮品
senses.example: The menu marks which drinks are alcoholic.
senses.exampleCN: 菜单标出了哪些饮品含酒精。
senses.why: Alcohol plus the adjective suffix -ic means having the nature of alcohol: the drink carries the substance inside it.
senses.whyCN: alcohol 加形容词后缀 -ic，意为「具有酒精性质的」：饮品把这个物质带在里面。

senses.title: A person dependent on drinking
senses.definition: a person who is unable to control their drinking and depends on alcohol
senses.definitionCN: 无法控制饮酒、依赖酒精的人
senses.example: The programme helps alcoholics rebuild their daily routines.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目帮助酗酒者重建日常生活。
senses.why: The same adjective became a noun for the person whose life is shaped by the substance, a common pattern in medical English.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词转成名词，指生活被这种物质塑造的人，这是医学英语里常见的构词方式。

senses.title: Caused by alcohol
senses.definition: describing a disease or condition caused by heavy drinking
senses.definitionCN: 形容由大量饮酒引起的疾病或状况
senses.example: He was treated for alcoholic liver disease.
senses.exampleCN: 他因酒精性肝病接受治疗。
senses.why: Here -ic marks origin rather than content: the illness is not made of alcohol but produced by it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 -ic 标的是来源而不是内容：这种病不是由酒精构成，而是由酒精造成。

intro.en: Alcoholic is alcohol with a Latin adjective ending, first used for the substance and then for the person.
intro.cn: alcoholic 是 alcohol 加拉丁形容词词尾，先用于物质，再用于人。

items.en: The base word began as Arabic al-kuḥl, a fine antimony powder.
items.cn: 基础词最初是阿拉伯语 al-kuḥl，一种细锑粉。

items.en: Medieval Latin alcohol meant a refined powder or essence.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alcohol 指提炼的细粉或精华。

items.en: English alcohol came to mean the spirit of wine and then intoxicating drink.
items.cn: 英语 alcohol 先指酒之精华，后指醉人的饮品。

items.en: The suffix -ic, from Latin -icus, means belonging to or having the nature of.
items.cn: 后缀 -ic 来自拉丁语 -icus，意为「属于……的、具有……性质的」。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in the nineteenth century, when chemistry and medicine were naming substances precisely.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十九世纪有记录，当时化学与医学正在为物质精确命名。

items.en: Medical writing then turned the adjective into a noun for the dependent patient.
items.cn: 医学写作随后把这个形容词转为名词，指依赖酒精的病人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the alcohol family; the near-meaning group gathers words for people who drink too much.
note.cn: 形近组收 alcohol 词族；近义组收指过量饮酒者的词。

entries.definition: The substance itself, ethanol or drinks containing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指物质本身，即乙醇或含乙醇的饮品。

entries.definition: The condition of dependence on alcohol.
entries.definitionCN: 指对酒精产生依赖的状况。

entries.definition: Containing no alcohol at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指完全不含酒精的。

entries.definition: An old, blunt word for someone who drinks too much.
entries.definitionCN: 指过量饮酒者的一个古老而直白的说法。

entries.definition: A person physically or mentally dependent on a substance.
entries.definitionCN: 指在生理或心理上依赖某种物质的人。

entries.definition: Someone who drinks a lot but is not necessarily dependent.
entries.definitionCN: 指饮酒很多但未必已成瘾的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the adjective and the noun apart by asking what the word is attached to.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子通过追问这个词挂在什么上，把形容词与名词分开。

normal.en: An alcoholic drink contains the substance; an alcoholic person is controlled by it.
normal.cn: alcoholic drink 含有这种物质；alcoholic person 被这种物质控制。

normal.en: The suffix -ic means having the nature of, so alcoholic means alcohol-like or alcohol-filled.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ic 意为「具有……性质」，所以 alcoholic 意为「像酒精的、充满酒精的」。

normal.en: Alcoholic liver disease is named by its cause, not by its content.
normal.cn: alcoholic liver disease 是按病因命名，而不是按内容物命名。

normal.en: Recovering alcoholic is a phrase of hope: the dependence is admitted but not accepted as permanent.
normal.cn: recovering alcoholic 是一个带希望的说法：承认依赖，但不认为它永久。

normal.en: Nonalcoholic is the word to look for when you want a drink without the substance.
normal.cn: 想要不含这种物质的饮品时，要找的词就是 nonalcoholic。

abstract.en: Picture a glass with a small flame inside it, and a hand that cannot put the glass down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子里燃着小火，一只手放不下这只杯子。

abstract.en: The flame is the substance; the hand is the person; the same adjective can name either.
abstract.cn: 火是物质，手是人，同一个形容词可以指其中任何一个。

abstract.en: Put the glass on a clinic desk and the adjective becomes a diagnosis.
abstract.cn: 把杯子放到诊所桌上，这个形容词就变成一项诊断。

examples.en: This beer is alcoholic, so it is not for children.
examples.cn: 这种啤酒含酒精，不适合孩子。

examples.en: He has been a recovering alcoholic for six years.
examples.cn: 他已经戒酒六年了。

examples.en: The doctor warned him about alcoholic liver disease.
examples.cn: 医生警告他注意酒精性肝病。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱儿喝利克」——爱儿喝得厉害，成了酗酒者

root: alcohol（酒精，源自阿拉伯语 al-kuḥl）加拉丁形容词后缀 -ic（具有……性质的）；先指「含酒精的」，后名词化指「酒精成瘾者」。

sensesIntro.en: Two adjective senses describe drink and disease, and one noun sense names the dependent person.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个形容词义项分别描述饮品与疾病，一个名词义项命名依赖酒精的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass still holds a flame, and the hand holding it will not let go.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯子里仍燃着一团火，握着杯子的手却不肯松开。

branches.en: THE GLASS: the adjective first tells you what is inside the drink.
branches.cn: 杯子线：这个形容词首先告诉你杯里有什么。

branches.en: THE HAND: the same adjective then names the person who cannot let go.
branches.cn: 手线：同一个形容词随后命名那个放不下杯子的人。

branches.en: THE BODY: medical usage marks diseases that the substance has caused.
branches.cn: 身体线：医学用法标出由这种物质造成的疾病。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: the noun becomes a diagnosis and a label used in treatment.
branches.cn: 诊所线：名词变成诊断，也成为治疗中使用的标签。

branches.en: THE LINE: the same ending -ic ties the drink and the drinker into one family.
branches.cn: 词尾线：同一个 -ic 把饮品与饮者系进同一个词族。

intro.en: Alcoholic is a transparent suffix build on alcohol, and the -ic ending does most of the grammatical work.
intro.cn: alcoholic 是在 alcohol 上透明地加后缀构成，-ic 词尾承担了大部分语法工作。

latinIntro.en: The suffix is Latin, but the base is Arabic, so the Latin entry list stays short.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀来自拉丁语，词基却来自阿拉伯语，因此拉丁条目很短。

items.example: Alcohol is sold to adults only.
items.exampleCN: 酒精饮品只卖给成年人。
这家旅馆供应含酒精饮品。
酒精性肝病是可以预防的。

definition_zh: 代数；代数学；代数体系
definition_en: a branch of mathematics in which letters and symbols stand for unknown numbers
core_image: 黑板上字母代替未知数，等式像天平两边保持平衡
scene: 老师把未知数写成字母，让学生一步步解出它的值。In algebra, letters stand for numbers we do not yet know.
sceneCN: 这里 algebra 是「代数」（第 1 个义项：用符号代替数的数学分支）；句意为在代数里，字母代表我们还不知道的数。

pos.zh: 名词：代数；代数学；代数体系

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「代数的；代数式的」
由 algebraic 加 -ly 构成，义为「用代数方法地」
由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「代数学家」

senses.title: The branch of mathematics
senses.definition: the branch of mathematics that uses letters and symbols to represent numbers and solve equations
senses.definitionCN: 用字母和符号表示数并解方程的数学分支
senses.example: She started studying algebra at the age of twelve.
senses.exampleCN: 她十二岁开始学代数。
senses.why: The Arabic name meant the reunion of broken parts, and the subject is exactly that: pieces of a problem are put back together through symbols.
senses.whyCN: 这个阿拉伯语名称意为「破碎部分的重聚」，而这门学科做的正是这件事：用符号把问题的碎片重新拼合。

senses.title: A system of symbolic rules
senses.definition: a particular system of symbols and operations, such as Boolean algebra or linear algebra
senses.definitionCN: 一套特定的符号与运算体系，如布尔代数或线性代数
senses.example: Boolean algebra uses two values, true and false.
senses.exampleCN: 布尔代数使用真与假两个值。
senses.why: Once the method exists, each set of rules can be called an algebra, the way each language has its own grammar.
senses.whyCN: 方法一旦存在，每一套规则都可以称为一种代数，就像每种语言都有自己的语法。

senses.title: Schoolwork with unknowns
senses.definition: the school activity of solving problems with unknown quantities represented by letters
senses.definitionCN: 用字母代表未知量来解题的学校课业
senses.example: He spent the evening doing algebra before the test.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前他一晚上都在做代数题。
senses.why: In everyday school talk the subject name also names the exercise, because the practice is the subject for the student.
senses.whyCN: 在日常校园说法里，学科名也指练习题，因为对学生而言，做题就是这门学科。

intro.en: Algebra carries an Arabic name for restoring broken pieces, a name that describes the method itself.
intro.cn: algebra 带着一个阿拉伯语名称，意为「修复破碎的部分」，这个名称描述的正是方法本身。

items.en: Arabic al-jabr meant the restoring or reunion of broken parts, a term used for setting broken bones.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-jabr 意为修复或重聚破碎的部分，也曾用于接骨。

items.en: The root jabr supplied the idea of forcing something back into place, which became the operation of moving terms across an equation.
items.cn: 词根 jabr 提供「把某物强行归位」的观念，后来成为等式两边移项运算的名称。

items.en: Medieval Latin borrowed the term as algebra, the name of the calculation method in Arabic mathematics.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语借入作 algebra，指阿拉伯数学中这套计算方法的名称。

items.en: Old French passed the word to English, where it named the new art of calculation with unknowns.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词传给英语，用来命名用未知数计算的新技艺。

items.en: English algebra is recorded in the sixteenth century, first as the name of the method rather than the school subject.
items.cn: 英语 algebra 在十六世纪有记录，最初指方法名称，而不是学校科目。

items.en: Modern mathematics widened the word to cover many symbolic systems, from linear to abstract algebra.
items.cn: 现代数学扩大了这个词，使之涵盖从线性代数到抽象代数的众多符号体系。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the algebra family; the near-meaning group gathers neighbouring branches of mathematics.
note.cn: 形近组收 algebra 词族；近义组收相邻的数学分支。

entries.definition: Relating to algebra or to symbolic calculation.
entries.definitionCN: 指与代数或符号计算有关的。

entries.definition: By means of algebra rather than by a graph.
entries.definitionCN: 指用代数方法而不是用图象来解。

entries.definition: A person who works on algebra.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究代数的人。

entries.definition: The basic mathematics of numbers and ordinary operations.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于数与普通运算的基础数学。

entries.definition: The mathematics of shape, size and position.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于形状、大小与位置的数学。

entries.definition: The mathematics of continuous change, built on algebra.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究连续变化的数学，建立在代数之上。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the Arabic meaning of reuniting pieces to the visible work of solving.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把阿拉伯语「重聚碎片」的含义，系到看得见的解题动作上。

normal.en: Algebra literally means reuniting broken parts, which is what moving terms does.
normal.cn: algebra 字面意思是把破碎部分重新拼合，这正是移项在做的事。

normal.en: Letters stand in for numbers, so an equation is a sentence with blank spaces.
normal.cn: 字母代替数字，所以一个等式就是一句留有空格的句子。

normal.en: Linear algebra is the algebra of lines and vectors.
normal.cn: linear algebra 是线和向量的代数。

normal.en: Boolean algebra borrows the method for true and false instead of numbers.
normal.cn: 布尔代数把同一方法借去处理真与假，而不是数字。

normal.en: An algebra problem is a broken bone of numbers, waiting to be set back into place.
normal.cn: 一道代数题就是数字的断骨，等着被接回原位。

abstract.en: Picture a broken plate on a table, with the pieces numbered and scattered.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上有一只碎盘子，碎片编号后散落着。

abstract.en: Each equation is a rule for which pieces may be moved next to which.
abstract.cn: 每个等式都是一条规则，说明哪块碎片可以挪到哪块旁边。

abstract.en: When the pieces fit again, the value of the unknown appears in the last joint.
abstract.cn: 碎片重新合上时，未知数的值就显现在最后一道接缝里。

examples.en: Algebra taught her to solve for an unknown step by step.
examples.cn: 代数教会她一步步解出未知数。

examples.en: The engineer used linear algebra to model the bridge.
examples.cn: 工程师用线性代数给这座桥建模。

examples.en: He found the algebra test harder than geometry.
examples.cn: 他觉得代数测验比几何难。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「二姐不惹」——二姐不惹代数题，一见字母就头疼

root: 源自阿拉伯语 al-jabr「修复、重聚破碎部分」（原也指接骨），经中世纪拉丁语 algebra 与古法语 algebre 进入英语；指用符号把问题的碎片重新拼合的数学方法。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses move from the mathematical branch, to a particular symbolic system, to the school exercise that teaches it.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从数学分支，走到特定的符号体系，再到教授这门学问的学校练习。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: broken pieces lie on a table, and a rule tells you how to join them until the missing piece appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：破碎的片块散在桌上，一条规则告诉你怎么把它们接起来，直到缺失的一块现身。

branches.en: THE BONES: the Arabic name came from setting broken bones, and the subject still sets pieces back in place.
branches.cn: 接骨线：这个阿拉伯语名称来自接骨，而这门学科仍把碎片接回原位。

branches.en: THE LETTER: a symbol takes the place of a number we do not know yet.
branches.cn: 字母线：一个符号代替我们还不知道的数。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: each set of symbols and operations becomes an algebra of its own.
branches.cn: 体系线：每一套符号与运算都成为它自己的一种代数。

branches.en: THE CLASSROOM: the name slides from the subject to the exercises done at a desk.
branches.cn: 课堂线：名称从学科滑到课桌上做的练习题。

branches.en: THE RULE: what all algebras share is a rule for moving symbols without changing the balance.
branches.cn: 规则线：所有代数共享的是同一类规则，在不破坏平衡的前提下移动符号。

intro.en: Algebra is an Arabic loanword with a productive English suffix family; the compounds name branches of the subject.
intro.cn: algebra 是阿拉伯语借词，英语给它长出了能产的后缀词族；复合词则命名各分支。

latinIntro.en: The word reached English through medieval Latin, but its base is Arabic, so Latin family entries are limited.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经中世纪拉丁语进入英语，但词基来自阿拉伯语，因此拉丁同族条目有限。

items.meaningCN: 用符号表示未知数的数学
items.example: Algebra is taught in middle school.
The Arabic term also meant bone setting.
items.exampleCN: 这个阿拉伯语词也曾指接骨。

items.example: It forms algebraical, an older variant.
items.exampleCN: 它构成较早的变体 algebraical。

items.example: Linear algebra is used in computer graphics.
items.exampleCN: 线性代数用于计算机图形学。

items.meaning: algebra of true and false values
items.exampleCN: 布尔代数是数字电路的基础。

definition_zh: 相像的；相似的；同样地；一视同仁地
definition_en: similar to each other, or in the same way
core_image: 两面镜子面对面，镜中的两张脸几乎分不出差别
scene: 双胞胎穿上同样的校服，老师一时分不清谁是谁。The two sisters look so much alike that their teacher mixes them up.
sceneCN: 这里 alike 是「相像的」（第 1 个义项：彼此相似的）；句意为两姐妹长得太像，老师会把她们认错。

pos.zh: 形容词：相像的；相似的（多作表语）
副词：同样地；一视同仁地

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「相像；相似」，较为少见
由否定前缀 un- 加本词构成，义为「不相似的」
与 alike 同源的基础词，义为「像；如同」

senses.title: Similar to each other
senses.definition: looking or being similar to one another, used after a linking verb
senses.definitionCN: 彼此在外观或性质上相似，多用在系动词之后
senses.example: The twins are alike in voice but not in temper.
senses.exampleCN: 这对双胞胎声音相像，脾气却不同。
senses.why: Old English gelīc joined ge- with līc, the word for body or form, so alike originally meant having the same form as another.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gelīc 把 ge- 与表示身体、形体的 līc 结合，所以 alike 原意为「与另一者具有相同形体」。

senses.title: In the same way
senses.definition: in the same manner, without difference in treatment
senses.definitionCN: 以相同方式，不加区别地对待
senses.example: The law treats rich and poor alike.
senses.exampleCN: 法律对富人和穷人一视同仁。
senses.why: The adjective's idea of shared form becomes an adverb of shared treatment: the same rule is applied to every case.
senses.whyCN: 形容词「共有同一形体」的观念转成副词的「共有同一待遇」：同一条规则适用于每个情况。

intro.en: Alike is an Old English word whose second half meant body or form, and it has lost the endings it once had.
intro.cn: alike 是古英语词，后半部分原指身体或形体，它曾有的词形变化后来都消失了。

items.en: Old English gelīc meant having the same form or appearance as another.
items.cn: 古英语 gelīc 意为「与另一者具有相同形体或外观」。

items.en: The prefix ge- expressed togetherness, so the word began with the idea of two things sharing a shape.
items.cn: 前缀 ge- 表达「共同」，所以这个词一开始就带有两物共享一个形体的观念。

items.en: Līc meant body or form, and it survives in the suffix -ly and in the word like.
items.cn: līc 意为身体或形体，它活在后缀 -ly 和单词 like 里。

items.en: The modern form alike emerged, keeping the sense of resemblance but dropping most inflections.
items.cn: 现代形式 alike 出现，保留相似含义，却丢掉了大部分词形变化。

items.en: Because the word described a shared state, English kept it after the verb rather than before the noun.
items.cn: 因为这个词描述一种共有状态，英语把它留在动词之后，而不是名词之前。

items.en: The adverb use, as in treat them alike, grew from the same idea of one form applied to all.
items.cn: 副词用法如 treat them alike，也由同一个「同一形式施于所有」的观念长出。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same body-form root; the near-meaning group gathers words of resemblance.
note.cn: 形近组收来自同一「形体」词根的词；近义组收表示相似的词。

entries.definition: Similar to, or in the manner of; the base word behind alike.
entries.definitionCN: 指与……相似，或以……方式；是 alike 背后的基础词。

entries.definition: Probable, from the sense of having a similar appearance to truth.
entries.definitionCN: 指很可能的，来自「与真相外观相似」的含义。

entries.definition: The state of looking like someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 指看起来像某人或某物的状态。

entries.definition: Not similar to each other.
entries.definitionCN: 指彼此不相似的。

entries.definition: Resembling but not identical, the general word for partial likeness.
entries.definitionCN: 指相似但不相同，是表示部分相像的通用词。

entries.definition: Exactly the same in every detail.
entries.definitionCN: 指每个细节都完全相同。

entries.definition: Similar enough to be measured or judged against each other.
entries.definitionCN: 指相似到可以相互比较或评判。

entries.definition: One and the same thing, stronger than merely similar.
entries.definitionCN: 指同一个事物，比「仅仅相似」更强。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the twin image and the two grammar positions alike can take.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子用双胞胎意象，以及 alike 能站的两个语法位置。

normal.en: Alike means having the same body or form, so twins are its natural picture.
normal.cn: alike 意为具有相同身体或形体，所以双胞胎是它最自然的画面。

normal.en: Keep alike after the verb: the two are alike, not the alike two.
normal.cn: 把 alike 放在动词之后：the two are alike，而不是 the alike two。

normal.en: Treat them alike means apply one rule to both, not that both are the same person.
normal.cn: treat them alike 意为对两者用同一条规则，而不是说两者是同一个人。

normal.en: Look alike is about appearance; think alike is about the mind.
normal.cn: look alike 说的是外表；think alike 说的是心思。

normal.en: Exactly alike leaves no difference at all, while much alike still leaves some.
normal.cn: exactly alike 不留任何差别，much alike 仍留有一些差别。

abstract.en: Picture two mirrors facing each other, each holding a copy of the room.
abstract.cn: 想象两面镜子相对而立，每一面都映出这个房间的一份副本。

abstract.en: The copies are not the same object, but they share one shape, and that shared shape is alike.
abstract.cn: 两个副本不是同一件东西，却共有一个形状，这个共有的形状就是 alike。

abstract.en: Now replace the mirrors with two people and the shared shape becomes a family resemblance.
abstract.cn: 把镜子换成两个人，共有的形状就成了一脉相承的相像。

examples.en: The two brothers look alike but walk very differently.
examples.cn: 两兄弟长得很像，走路的姿态却大不相同。

examples.en: Rules should apply alike to every student.
examples.cn: 规则应当同样适用于每个学生。

examples.en: Her handwriting and her mother's are remarkably alike.
examples.cn: 她的字迹和她母亲的惊人地相像。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额来客」——额，来客长得和主人一个样

root: 古英语 gelīc，由 ge-（共同）加 līc（身体、形体）构成，原意为「具有相同形体」；现代英语中多作表语形容词与副词。

sensesIntro.en: One sense describes shared appearance, the other shared treatment; both come from the same idea of one form.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项描述共有的外观，另一个义项描述共有的待遇；两者都来自「同一形体」的观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people stand side by side, and the outline of one fits the outline of the other almost exactly.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人并肩而立，一个人的轮廓几乎正好套住另一个人的轮廓。

branches.en: THE OUTLINE: the oldest sense is a shared shape, and the body word līc is still inside it.
branches.cn: 轮廓线：最古老的义项是共有的形状，表示身体的 līc 仍藏在词里。

branches.en: THE PAIR: the word needs at least two things, because resemblance is a relation.
branches.cn: 成对线：这个词至少需要两个东西，因为相像是一种关系。

branches.en: THE RULE: shared form becomes shared treatment when a law applies the same measure to all.
branches.cn: 规则线：当法律把同一尺度用于所有人，共有形体就变成共有待遇。

branches.en: THE VERB SLOT: English keeps the word after the verb because it names a state, not a permanent class.
branches.cn: 动词后线：英语把这个词放在动词之后，因为它命名状态，而不是永久类别。

branches.en: THE MIRROR: both senses work like a mirror, one showing shape and one showing equal treatment.
branches.cn: 镜子线：两个义项都像镜子，一个照出形状，一个照出平等对待。

intro.en: Alike is a native Old English formation, so its affixes are native prefixes and suffixes rather than Latin ones.
intro.cn: alike 是本土古英语构词，所以它的构词成分是本土前后缀，而不是拉丁前后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the word belongs to the Old English layer, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基；这个词属于古英语层，因此拉丁条目为空。

items.example: It began the older form gelīc.
items.exampleCN: 它是较早形式 gelīc 的开头。
它活在 like 与 -ly 中。
它构成 friendly 与 likely。

definition_zh: 活着的；有活力的；仍然存在的；意识到的
definition_en: living and not dead; full of energy; still in existence; aware of something
core_image: 胸口起伏、眼睛发亮的一具身体，与静止的雕像形成对照
scene: 地震后第三天，救援队从瓦砾下抬出一个还在呼吸的孩子。Rescuers found the missing hiker still alive after four days.
sceneCN: 这里 alive 是「活着的」（第 1 个义项：未死亡的）；句意为救援队发现失踪的徒步者在四天后仍然活着。

pos.zh: 形容词：活着的；有活力的；仍然存在的；意识到的（多作表语）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「活着；活力」，较为少见
与 alive 同源，义为「活的；现场直播的」
由 life 加 -ly 构成，义为「活泼的；生动的」
由 lively 逆构而成，义为「使活跃起来」

senses.title: Living, not dead
senses.definition: having life; not dead
senses.definitionCN: 有生命的；未死亡的
senses.example: The fish was still alive when they pulled it from the net.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把鱼从网里捞出来时，鱼还活着。
senses.why: The word began as the phrase on life: to be alive was to be in life, a state rather than a permanent quality.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是短语 on life：be alive 就是「在生命之中」，是一种状态，而不是永久属性。

senses.title: Full of energy
senses.definition: energetic, lively, or responsive in a way that feels full of life
senses.definitionCN: 精力充沛、活泼或反应敏锐，给人充满生命的感觉
senses.example: The market comes alive early on Saturday mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 星期六清早，市场就活跃起来。
senses.why: If being alive is being in life, a place or person can seem to enter that state, and the word extends to energy.
senses.whyCN: 如果活着就是置身生命之中，一个地方或一个人也能显得进入了这种状态，词义便延伸到活力。

senses.title: Still in existence
senses.definition: continuing to exist or be used, not forgotten or ended
senses.definitionCN: 继续存在或被使用，未被遗忘或终止
senses.example: The old tradition is still alive in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 这项古老传统在村里仍然活着。
senses.why: Customs are treated as living things: a tradition that still moves people has not died, so it is alive.
senses.whyCN: 习俗被当作活物：一条仍能打动人的传统没有死，所以它仍然 alive。

senses.title: Aware of something
senses.definition: conscious of or sensitive to a fact or danger, as in alive to
senses.definitionCN: 意识到或敏感于某个事实或危险，用于 alive to
senses.example: Good managers stay alive to changes in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 优秀的管理者会对市场变化保持警觉。
senses.why: To be alive to something is to have one's senses open to it, the same wakefulness that keeps a body alive.
senses.whyCN: be alive to 某事物，就是让感官对它敞开，这与维持身体存活的是同一种清醒。

intro.en: Alive is a phrase that became a word: on life turned into one adjective of state.
intro.cn: alive 是一个由短语凝固成的词：on life 变成一个表状态的形容词。

items.en: Old English expressed the state with the phrase on līfe, literally in life.
items.cn: 古英语用短语 on līfe 表达这一状态，字面为「在生命之中」。

items.en: Līf meant life, and it became the modern noun life.
items.cn: līf 意为生命，后来变成现代名词 life。

items.en: The phrase merged into the single word alive, with a- functioning as an old preposition.
items.cn: 短语合成了单词 alive，其中 a- 起古老介词的作用。

items.en: English kept alive as a predicative adjective, so we say the patient is alive, not an alive patient.
items.cn: 英语把 alive 保持为表语形容词，所以我们说病人 is alive，而不说 an alive patient。

items.en: The sense of being lively or animated grew from the physical state into a description of atmosphere.
items.cn: 「有活力」的义项从身体状态扩展到对气氛的描述。

items.en: The phrase alive to extended life into attention: the senses are awake to something.
items.cn: 短语 alive to 把生命延伸到注意力：感官对某事物保持清醒。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same life stem; the near-meaning group gathers states of being alive.
note.cn: 形近组收来自同一「生命」词干的词；近义组收表示存活状态的词。

entries.definition: To have life, or an adjective meaning not dead or broadcast in real time.
entries.definitionCN: 指拥有生命，或作形容词表示活的、现场直播的。

entries.definition: Full of energy and quick to respond.
entries.definitionCN: 指精力充沛、反应敏捷的。

entries.definition: The participle and adjective meaning currently alive.
entries.definitionCN: 指分词兼形容词，表示当前活着的。

entries.definition: To make something more active or cheerful.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某事物更活跃或更欢快。

entries.definition: Not dead, often used before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指未死亡的，常放在名词之前。

entries.definition: Having the quality of life, opposed to inanimate objects.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有生命特性的，与无生命物体相对。

entries.definition: Still taking air, the plain physical sign of life.
entries.definitionCN: 指仍在呼吸，是生命最直白的身体迹象。

entries.definition: Awake and aware, closer to the alive to sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指清醒且有意识，更接近 alive to 的义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the phrase in life to the energy of a room and the alertness of a mind.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从「在生命之中」这个短语，走到房间的活力与头脑的警觉。

normal.en: Alive was once on life: to be alive is to be inside life.
normal.cn: alive 曾经是 on life：活着就是置身生命之中。

normal.en: Keep the word after the verb: the patient is alive, not the alive patient.
normal.cn: 把这个词放在动词之后：the patient is alive，而不是 the alive patient。

normal.en: Come alive describes a place or scene gaining energy, not a dead body returning.
normal.cn: come alive 描述地方或场景获得活力，不是尸体复活。

normal.en: A tradition is alive when it still moves people.
normal.cn: 一条传统仍能打动人时，它就是 alive。

normal.en: Alive to danger means your senses are open in that direction.
normal.cn: alive to danger 意为你的感官朝那个方向敞开着。

abstract.en: Picture a flame inside a glass box, and beside it a stone statue of the same shape.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃罩里有一团火，旁边是一尊同样形状的石像。

abstract.en: The flame moves, feeds, and changes; the stone keeps the outline but not the state.
abstract.cn: 火在动、在消耗、在变化；石头保留了轮廓，却没有那种状态。

abstract.en: Alive is the name of that state, not of the outline.
abstract.cn: alive 命名的正是这种状态，而不是那个轮廓。

examples.en: The old tree is still alive after the fire.
examples.cn: 大火之后那棵老树仍然活着。

examples.en: The party came alive when the music started.
examples.cn: 音乐一响，聚会就活跃起来。

examples.en: She is alive to the risks of the new plan.
examples.cn: 她对这项新计划的风险保持警觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额赖夫」——额，赖夫还活着，喘着气

root: 古英语短语 on līfe（在生命之中）凝固而成，a- 为古老介词，līf 即现代 life；因此 alive 是表语形容词，表示「处于生命状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses extend one state: being in life, showing energy, continuing to exist, and having the senses awake.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项延伸同一种状态：置身生命、显露活力、继续存在，以及感官清醒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chest rises and falls, and beside it a stone statue of the same shape stays perfectly still.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具胸膛起伏着，旁边同样形状的石像却一动不动。

branches.en: THE BREATH: the first sense is the plain physical state of not being dead.
branches.cn: 呼吸线：第一个义项是未死亡这一直白的身体状态。

branches.en: THE SPARK: a person or place can show the same state as visible energy.
branches.cn: 火花线：一个人或一个地方能把同一种状态表现为可见的活力。

branches.en: THE TRADITION: what still moves people is treated as not having died.
branches.cn: 传统线：仍能打动人的东西被当作没有死去。

branches.en: THE SENSE: being alive to something is keeping attention awake in one direction.
branches.cn: 感官线：be alive to 某事物，就是让注意力朝一个方向保持清醒。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: the word always implies a possible opposite, the statue or the grave.
branches.cn: 对照线：这个词总暗含一个可能的反面，石像或坟墓。

intro.en: Alive is a native phrase-word, and its larger family comes from life rather than from suffixes added to alive itself.
intro.cn: alive 是本土短语凝固成的词，它更大的词族来自 life，而不是加在 alive 本身上的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is wholly Old English, so there are no Latin entries for it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词完全属于古英语，所以没有拉丁条目。

items.example: It came from the phrase on life.

items.meaning: to be alive, or not dead

items.example: The street is lively at night.
Music can liven a dull room.
items.exampleCN: 音乐能让沉闷的房间活跃起来。

items.example: The missing dog was found alive and well.
items.exampleCN: 走失的狗被找到时安然无恙。

definition_zh: 全部的；所有的；一切；全体；完全
definition_en: every member or part of a group, the whole of something, or completely
core_image: 一张桌上摆满所有盘子，一个也不缺
scene: 雨停后，整条街的孩子都跑出来踩水。All the children ran outside when the rain stopped.
sceneCN: 这里 all 是「全部的」（第 1 个义项：限定词，指某一群体的每一个成员）；句意为雨停后所有孩子都跑到外面。

pos.zh: 限定词：所有的；全部的
代词：全部；一切；所有人
副词：完全；十分
名词：全部；一切

derivatives.zh: 由 all 与 ready 构成的复合副词，义为「已经」
由 all 与 so 构成的复合副词，义为「也；还」
由 all 与 though 构成的复合连词，义为「虽然」
由 all 与 together 构成的复合副词，义为「完全；总共」
由 all 与 mighty 构成的复合形容词，义为「全能的」

senses.title: Every member of a group
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean every member or part of the group, with no exception
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示该群体的每一个成员或部分，无一例外
senses.example: All the seats were taken before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 中午之前所有座位都被占满了。
senses.why: Old English eall meant the whole of a set, and as a determiner it still insists that no member is left out.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 eall 意为一个集合的整体，作限定词时它仍坚持不落下任何一个成员。

senses.title: Everything taken together
senses.definition: the whole of something, or every person or thing being considered, used as a pronoun
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的整体，或正在考虑的所有人或物，作代词使用
senses.example: All of the money was spent on repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 所有的钱都花在维修上了。
senses.why: The same whole appears without a following noun: the group is already known, so the pronoun points at it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个整体不再带后面的名词：群体已经明确，于是代词直接指向它。

senses.title: Completely
senses.definition: used to emphasize that something is entirely the case, as in all alone or all too easy
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调某事完全如此，如 all alone 或 all too easy
senses.example: He was all alone in the empty house.
senses.exampleCN: 他独自一人待在那栋空房子里。
senses.why: The whole set becomes a degree: if every part is affected, the effect is complete, and the word turns into an intensifier.
senses.whyCN: 整体变成了程度：如果每一部分都受影响，效果就是完全的，于是这个词变成强调词。

senses.title: One's whole effort or possession
senses.definition: everything a person has or can give, as in give one's all
senses.definitionCN: 一个人拥有或能付出的一切，用于 give one's all
senses.example: She gave her all to the final performance.
senses.exampleCN: 她把全部心力都投入到最后一场演出。
senses.why: Here all is a noun standing for a total that a person pours out, the set treated as a single offering.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 all 是名词，代表一个人倾尽的总量，把整个集合当作一份献礼。

intro.en: All is one of the oldest English words, and its many compounds show how long it has been building new meanings.
intro.cn: all 是英语最古老的词之一，它众多的复合词说明它建构新义已有很久。

items.en: Old English eall meant the whole, entire, or every, and it was inflected for case and number.
items.cn: 古英语 eall 意为整体的、全部的或每一个，并有格与数的变化。

items.en: Middle English dropped most endings, leaving the single form all for every grammatical role.
items.cn: 中世纪英语丢掉大部分词尾，留下单一形式 all 承担各种语法角色。

items.en: The word began to stand alone as a pronoun for a group already mentioned.
items.cn: 这个词开始单独作代词，指已经提到的群体。

items.en: English built already, also, although and altogether by fusing all with a second word.
items.cn: 英语把 all 与第二个词融合，造出 already、also、although 与 altogether。

items.en: The intensifying use, as in all alone, grew from the sense of a complete state.
items.cn: all alone 这类强调用法，从「完整状态」的含义长出。

items.en: All remains a closed-class word: few new senses appear, but the old ones spread across many phrases.
items.cn: all 仍是封闭类词：新义很少出现，旧义却铺展到大量短语中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers all's own compounds; the near-meaning group gathers words for wholeness.
note.cn: 形近组收 all 自己构成的复合词；近义组收表示整体的词。

entries.definition: Before now, or sooner than expected.
entries.definitionCN: 指在此之前，或比预期更早。

entries.definition: In addition; as well.
entries.definitionCN: 指另外；也。

entries.definition: Even though; despite the fact that.
entries.definitionCN: 指虽然；尽管。

entries.definition: Completely, or counting everything.
entries.definitionCN: 指完全地，或总共计算。

entries.definition: Complete as one unit, not divided or missing a part.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为一个整体完整，未分割或缺损。

entries.definition: The full extent of something, often more formal than all.
entries.definitionCN: 指某事物的全部范围，常比 all 更正式。

entries.definition: All things, used when the group is not named.
entries.definitionCN: 指所有事物，用于群体未被点名时。

entries.definition: The complete amount reached by adding parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指各部分相加得到的完整数量。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the whole-set image and show how a determiner becomes a pronoun, an adverb and a noun.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子守住「整套」意象，并展示限定词如何变成代词、副词和名词。

normal.en: All means no member left out, so the picture is a full table, not a big table.
normal.cn: all 意为不落下任何成员，所以画面是摆满的桌子，而不是大桌子。

normal.en: All the children is a determiner; all of them is a pronoun; both point at the same set.
normal.cn: all the children 是限定词；all of them 是代词；两者指向同一个集合。

normal.en: All alone uses all as an intensifier: completely alone.
normal.cn: all alone 把 all 用作强调词：完全独自一人。

normal.en: Give your all turns the whole set into a noun you can hand over.
normal.cn: give your all 把整个集合变成可以交出去的名词。

normal.en: Already, also, although and altogether are all plus a second word, grown into single units.
normal.cn: already、also、although 与 altogether 都是 all 加第二个词，长成了单词。

abstract.en: Picture a long table with a place set at every seat, and not one chair empty.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，每个座位都摆好了餐具，没有一把椅子是空的。

abstract.en: Remove the table and keep the fullness: that fullness is all.
abstract.cn: 把桌子拿走，只留下「满」：这份满就是 all。

abstract.en: Now let one person at the table give everything on it away, and all becomes a noun.
abstract.cn: 再让桌边一个人把桌上的一切都送出去，all 就变成名词。

examples.en: All the lights went out at the same moment.
examples.cn: 所有灯在同一刻熄灭。

examples.en: All of us agreed to wait until morning.
examples.cn: 我们全都同意等到早上。

examples.en: Above all, keep the children away from the river.
examples.cn: 最重要的是，让孩子们远离那条河。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，全部」——哦，全部都在，一个不少

root: 古英语 eall（整体的、全部的），本有格与数变化；中世纪英语词尾脱落，留下单一形式 all，并构成 already、also、although、altogether 等复合词。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses are one whole seen as a determiner, a pronoun, a degree, and a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项是同一个「整体」，分别被看作限定词、代词、程度和名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long table is fully set, and every chair has someone in it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌摆得满满当当，每一把椅子上都有人。

branches.en: THE SEAT: as a determiner the word checks every seat in the group.
branches.cn: 座位线：作限定词时，这个词逐一检查群体中的每个座位。

branches.en: THE GROUP: as a pronoun it points at the whole group already known.
branches.cn: 群体线：作代词时，它指向已经明确的整个群体。

branches.en: THE DEGREE: if every part is affected, the effect is complete, and the word intensifies.
branches.cn: 程度线：如果每一部分都受影响，效果就是完全的，这个词便用来强调。

branches.en: THE OFFERING: the whole set can become a noun, something a person gives away.
branches.cn: 献出线：整个集合可以变成名词，成为一个人交出去的东西。

branches.en: THE CLOSED CLASS: all rarely gains new senses; it changes grammar instead.
branches.cn: 封闭线：all 很少增加新义，它改变的是语法角色。

intro.en: All is a native word that mostly works by compounding, fusing with a second word to make a new adverb or conjunction.
intro.cn: all 是本土词，主要通过复合构词，与第二个词融合成新的副词或连词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base for all, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: all 没有拉丁词基，因此拉丁条目为空。

items.example: Although it rained, we went out.
items.exampleCN: 虽然下雨，我们还是出门了。
它构成 all-star 与 all-purpose。

definition_zh: 过敏的；对……过敏的；对……极反感的
definition_en: having a physical reaction to a substance, or strongly disliking something
core_image: 皮肤上突然浮起的红点，一碰到花粉就发痒
scene: 春天花粉飞扬，她一出门就不停打喷嚏。She is allergic to pollen and sneezes all through spring.
sceneCN: 这里 allergic 是「过敏的」（第 1 个义项：对某物质产生身体过敏反应）；句意为她对花粉过敏，整个春天都在打喷嚏。

pos.zh: 形容词：过敏的；对……极反感的

derivatives.zh: 去掉形容词后缀得到的基础名词，义为「过敏」
由 allergy 加 -gen 构成，义为「过敏原」
由 allergy 加 -ist 构成，义为「过敏科医生」
由 allergen 加 -ic 构成，义为「引起过敏的」

senses.title: Reacting physically to a substance
senses.definition: having an immune reaction such as sneezing, itching, or swelling after contact with a particular substance
senses.definitionCN: 接触某种特定物质后出现打喷嚏、发痒或肿胀等免疫反应
senses.example: My brother is allergic to peanuts.
senses.exampleCN: 我弟弟对花生过敏。
senses.why: Greek allos meant other and ergon meant work; allergy named the body working against an otherwise harmless other thing.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 allos 意为「别的」，ergon 意为「工作」；allergy 命名身体对一种本来无害的「他者」发起抵抗工作。

senses.title: Strongly disliking something
senses.definition: strongly averse to something, often in a humorous or emphatic way
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物强烈反感，常带幽默或强调语气
senses.example: He is allergic to meetings that last all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他对开一下午的会深恶痛绝。
senses.why: The body's rejection of a substance becomes a metaphor for the mind's rejection of an idea, and the reaction is equally automatic.
senses.whyCN: 身体对物质的排斥，被借喻为头脑对观念的排斥，而且反应同样自动。

senses.title: Caused by allergy
senses.definition: describing a disease or symptom produced by an allergic reaction
senses.definitionCN: 形容由过敏反应引起的疾病或症状
senses.example: The clinic treats children with allergic asthma.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所治疗患过敏性哮喘的儿童。
senses.why: In medical compounds the word marks cause rather than the sufferer: the asthma is not allergic, it is asthma caused by allergy.
senses.whyCN: 在医学复合词里，这个词标的是病因而不是患者：哮喘本身不过敏，而是由过敏引起的哮喘。

intro.en: Allergic is a twentieth-century medical coinage built from two Greek words and later borrowed by everyday speech.
intro.cn: allergic 是二十世纪的医学新造词，由两个希腊词构成，后来被日常语言借用。

items.en: Greek allos meant other or different, the first half of the coinage.
items.cn: 希腊语 allos 意为「别的、不同的」，是新造词的前半部分。

items.en: Greek ergon meant work or action, and it also gives English energy and ergonomic.
items.cn: 希腊语 ergon 意为工作或作用，也是英语 energy 与 ergonomic 的来源。

items.en: The physician Clemens von Pirquet coined allergy for the body's altered, over-reactive response to a foreign substance.
items.cn: 医生克莱门斯·冯·皮尔凯造出 allergy 一词，指身体对外来物质的改变了的过度反应。

items.en: English borrowed allergy in the early twentieth century as the medical term spread.
items.cn: 二十世纪初，随着医学术语传播，英语借入了 allergy。

items.en: The adjective allergic followed, formed with the Latin-derived suffix -ic.
items.cn: 形容词 allergic 随后出现，用源自拉丁语的 -ic 构成。

items.en: Later the word was extended to strong dislike, first in speech and then in dictionaries.
items.cn: 后来这个词被扩展到强烈反感，先出现在口语，再进入词典。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the allergy family; the near-meaning group gathers words for sensitivity and intolerance.
note.cn: 形近组收 allergy 词族；近义组收表示敏感与不耐受的词。

entries.definition: The medical condition behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指形容词背后的医学状况，即过敏。

entries.definition: A substance that triggers an allergic reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 指引发过敏反应的物质，即过敏原。

entries.definition: A doctor who treats allergies.
entries.definitionCN: 指治疗过敏的医生。

entries.definition: Able to cause an allergic reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够引起过敏反应的。

entries.definition: Reacting easily to a substance or situation, a broader word.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某物质或情境容易起反应，是更宽泛的词。

entries.definition: Unable to digest or accept a food or substance.
entries.definitionCN: 指无法消化或接受某种食物或物质。

entries.definition: Reacting more strongly than usual to a stimulus.
entries.definitionCN: 指对刺激的反应比平常更强烈。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek meaning other work and the visible signs of a reaction.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用希腊语「他者 + 工作」的含义，以及看得见的反应迹象。

normal.en: Allergy is other work: the body works against something that should be harmless.
normal.cn: allergy 是「他者的工作」：身体对本来无害的东西发起抵抗。

normal.en: Allergic to pollen means pollen starts that work, and the nose pays.
normal.cn: allergic to pollen 意为花粉启动这项工作，鼻子付出代价。

normal.en: Allergic reaction is the body's overreaction, not the substance's attack.
normal.cn: allergic reaction 是身体的过度反应，而不是物质的攻击。

normal.en: Allergic asthma is asthma caused by allergy, so read the compound from right to left.
normal.cn: allergic asthma 是由过敏引起的哮喘，所以要从右往左读这个复合词。

normal.en: Saying you are allergic to meetings borrows the body's automatic refusal for the mind.
normal.cn: 说自己对开会有过敏反应，是把身体的自动拒绝借给头脑使用。

abstract.en: Picture a quiet house where a harmless cat walks in, and every alarm in the walls goes off.
abstract.cn: 想象一间安静的屋子，一只无害的猫走进来，墙里所有警报同时响起。

abstract.en: Nothing in the cat changed; only the house's way of working changed.
abstract.cn: 猫没有变，变的只是屋子运作的方式。

abstract.en: Allergic is the name of that house, not the name of the cat.
abstract.cn: allergic 是那间屋子的名字，不是那只猫的名字。

examples.en: She is allergic to shellfish and carries medicine with her.
examples.cn: 她对贝类过敏，随身带着药。

examples.en: The doctor asked whether anyone in the family was allergic.
examples.cn: 医生问家里是否有人过敏。

examples.en: He is allergic to loud arguments in small rooms.
examples.cn: 他对小房间里的高声争吵极为反感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额了叽刻」——额，一碰花粉就叽叽刻刻打喷嚏，过敏了

root: 由希腊语 allos（别的、不同的）与 ergon（工作、作用）构成；一九零六年由医生皮尔凯造出 allergy，指身体对外来物质的过度反应，再加 -ic 构成形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses describe the body's reaction and the illness it causes; one extends the reaction to the mind's strong dislike.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项描述身体的反应与由此引起的疾病；一个义项把这种反应延伸到头脑的强烈反感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a harmless substance enters the body, and the body's defences treat it as an invader.
core.cn: 核心意象：一种无害物质进入身体，身体的防线却把它当作入侵者。

branches.en: THE OTHER: Greek allos marks the substance as foreign, and the body reacts to its foreignness.
branches.cn: 他者线：希腊语 allos 标出物质的外来性，身体正是对这种外来性起反应。

branches.en: THE WORK: ergon is the body's work, and allergy is that work turned against something harmless.
branches.cn: 工作线：ergon 是身体的运作，过敏就是这项运作反过来对付无害之物。

branches.en: THE DISEASE: medical compounds use the word to mark a cause, as in allergic asthma.
branches.cn: 疾病线：医学复合词用这个词标出病因，如过敏性哮喘。

branches.en: THE MIND: the body's automatic refusal becomes a metaphor for strong dislike.
branches.cn: 头脑线：身体的自动拒绝变成强烈反感的比喻。

branches.en: THE REFLEX: in both senses the reaction is fast and not chosen.
branches.cn: 反射线：无论哪个义项，反应都很快且非自愿。

intro.en: Allergic is a Greek-based medical word with a Latin-style adjective ending and a productive family around allergy.
intro.cn: allergic 是希腊词基的医学词，带拉丁式形容词词尾，并围绕 allergy 有能产词族。

latinIntro.en: The roots are Greek rather than Latin, so the Latin entries are limited to the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 词根来自希腊语而非拉丁语，因此拉丁条目只限形容词词尾。

items.example: It is the first half of allergy.
items.exampleCN: 它是 allergy 的前半部分。

items.example: It is the second half of allergy.
items.exampleCN: 它是 allergy 的后半部分。

items.meaning: the body's response to an allergen
items.example: The rash was an allergic reaction.

definition_zh: 小巷；窄街；小径；保龄球道；死胡同
definition_en: a narrow passage between buildings, a bowling lane, or a garden path
core_image: 两堵高墙夹出的一条窄缝，尽头才见一点光
scene: 孩子把球滚进两栋楼之间的窄巷，转身就跑。The cat dashed into a narrow alley between the two buildings.
sceneCN: 这里 alley 是「小巷」（第 1 个义项：建筑之间的狭窄通道）；句意为猫冲进两栋楼之间的窄巷。

pos.zh: 名词：小巷；窄街；小径；保龄球道

derivatives.zh: 由 alley 与 way 构成的复合名词，义为「小巷；窄道」
复合名词，义为「流浪猫」，指在巷子里讨生活的猫
复合名词，义为「保龄球馆」或「保龄球道」
复合名词，义为「死胡同」，也比喻没有前途的办法

senses.title: A narrow passage between buildings
senses.definition: a narrow street or passage running between or behind buildings
senses.definitionCN: 在建筑物之间或后方延伸的狭窄街道或通道
senses.example: They met in an alley behind the market.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在市场后面的一条小巷里见面。
senses.why: Old French alee meant a walking or a passage, from the verb to go; an alley is a route squeezed between walls.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 alee 意为行走或通道，来自表示「走」的动词；alley 就是被墙夹出来的一条路线。

senses.title: A bowling lane
senses.definition: the long narrow track down which a bowling ball is rolled
senses.definitionCN: 供保龄球滚向球瓶的长而窄的球道
senses.example: The ball curved across the alley and hit the last pin.
senses.exampleCN: 球斜穿过球道，击中了最后一只瓶。
senses.why: A bowling lane has exactly the shape of an alley: a long narrow strip with walls or gutters on both sides.
senses.whyCN: 保龄球道的形状正像一条小巷：长而窄，两侧有边沟或挡板。

senses.title: A garden path
senses.definition: a narrow path in a garden or park, often bordered by plants
senses.definitionCN: 花园或公园中的狭窄小径，常由植物镶边
senses.example: A gravel alley led from the gate to the roses.
senses.exampleCN: 一条碎石小径从门口通向玫瑰丛。
senses.why: The passage does not need buildings: any narrow way meant for walking can carry the name.
senses.whyCN: 通道不一定需要建筑：任何供人行走的窄路都能用这个名字。

senses.title: A blind alley: no way forward
senses.definition: a course of action that leads nowhere, from the image of a passage with no exit
senses.definitionCN: 指走不通的做法，来自没有出口的通道这一意象
senses.example: Endless testing was a blind alley for the research team.
senses.exampleCN: 无止境的测试对研究团队来说是条死胡同。
senses.why: A real alley can end at a wall; the mind borrows that wall for any plan that cannot continue.
senses.whyCN: 真实的小巷可以在墙前终止；头脑把那堵墙借给任何无法继续的计划。

intro.en: Alley comes from a French verb meaning to go, and its narrow shape then spread to bowling and to dead ends.
intro.cn: alley 来自一个意为「走」的法语动词，它狭窄的形状随后延伸到保龄球与死胡同。

items.en: Latin ambulare meant to walk about, and it is the distant source of alley and of amble.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ambulare 意为到处走动，是 alley 与 amble 的远源。

items.en: Old French aler meant to go, and its participle alee named a going or a passage.
items.cn: 古法语 aler 意为去、走，其分词形式 alee 指一次行走或一条通道。

items.en: Middle English took the word as aley, a narrow way for walking.
items.cn: 中世纪英语借入作 aley，指供行走的窄路。

items.en: The long narrow lane of a bowling game borrowed the shape and the name.
items.cn: 保龄球那长而窄的球道借用了这个形状，也借用了这个名字。

items.en: Garden paths used the word for any narrow walk bordered by plants.
items.cn: 花园小径用这个词指任何由植物镶边的窄走道。

items.en: The phrase blind alley extended the physical dead end into a failed plan.
items.cn: 短语 blind alley 把物理上的死胡同延伸到失败的计划。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers alley compounds; the near-meaning group gathers narrow ways and passages.
note.cn: 形近组收 alley 的复合词；近义组收狭窄的道路与通道。

entries.definition: A narrow passage, often between buildings.
entries.definitionCN: 指狭窄通道，常在建筑之间。

entries.definition: A stray cat that lives in streets and alleys.
entries.definitionCN: 指在街巷里生活的流浪猫。

entries.definition: A building or lane for bowling.
entries.definitionCN: 指打保龄球的场馆或球道。

entries.definition: A passage with no exit, or a plan that cannot succeed.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有出口的通道，或无法成功的计划。

entries.definition: A narrow road in the country or a marked strip of a wider road.
entries.definitionCN: 指乡间窄路，或宽路上划出的一条车道。

entries.definition: A way through or along which someone or something passes.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或物穿行而过的通道。

entries.definition: A track made by walking, often outdoors.
entries.definitionCN: 指走出来的小路，多在户外。

entries.definition: A long passage inside a building or between rooms.
entries.definitionCN: 指建筑内部或房间之间的长通道。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with the narrow gap and then stretch it into a bowling lane and a dead end.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子先抓住那条窄缝，再把它拉成保龄球道与死胡同。

normal.en: Alley is a walking passage squeezed between two walls, so narrowness is the core.
normal.cn: alley 是被两堵墙夹出来的行走通道，所以「窄」是核心。

normal.en: A bowling alley is an alley laid flat and given pins.
normal.cn: bowling alley 是把小巷放平，再摆上球瓶。

normal.en: A garden alley is the same narrow walk with flowers instead of walls.
normal.cn: 花园小径是同一种窄走道，只是把墙换成了花。

normal.en: A blind alley ends at a wall, so the phrase means a plan that cannot go on.
normal.cn: blind alley 终止于一堵墙，所以这个短语指无法继续的计划。

normal.en: An alley cat lives in the gaps between buildings, not in a house.
normal.cn: alley cat 住在建筑之间的缝隙里，而不是住在屋里。

abstract.en: Picture two high brick walls almost touching, with a thin strip of sky above them.
abstract.cn: 想象两堵高高的砖墙几乎相碰，上方只留一条细细的天空。

abstract.en: Lay the strip down horizontally and it becomes a lane with a ball rolling along it.
abstract.cn: 把这条缝横过来放平，它就成了一条有球滚过的球道。

abstract.en: Put a wall across the far end and the same strip becomes a blind alley.
abstract.cn: 在远端横上一堵墙，同一条缝就成了死胡同。

examples.en: The delivery van blocked the narrow alley behind the shop.
examples.cn: 送货的面包车堵住了商店后面的窄巷。

examples.en: They spent the afternoon at a bowling alley near the station.
examples.cn: 他们一下午都待在车站附近的保龄球馆。

examples.en: The committee realized the old plan was a blind alley.
examples.cn: 委员会意识到旧方案是一条死胡同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱理」——爱理不理，只肯走那条没人理的小巷

root: 经由古法语 alee（行走、通道）来自拉丁语 ambulare（走动）；本指两墙之间的窄路，后引申指保龄球道、花园小径，并以 blind alley 比喻无出路的办法。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses all keep the shape of a long narrow strip, filled with walls, gutters, plants, or a final barrier.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都保留「长而窄的一条」这个形状，只是填进去的是墙、边沟、植物或一道终点屏障。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two walls stand almost touching, and a thin line of light runs between them toward the far end.
core.cn: 核心意象：两堵墙几乎相贴，一线光在它们之间一直延伸到远端。

branches.en: THE GAP: the first sense is a way for people squeezed between buildings.
branches.cn: 缝隙线：第一个义项是人们在建筑之间挤过去的路。

branches.en: THE LANE: the same strip lies flat and becomes a track for a rolling ball.
branches.cn: 球道线：同一条窄带放平，就成了滚球的轨道。

branches.en: THE GARDEN: walls give way to plants, but the narrow walk remains.
branches.cn: 花园线：墙换成了植物，窄走道仍然保留。

branches.en: THE WALL: when the far end is closed, the passage becomes a metaphor for failure.
branches.cn: 墙线：远端被封住时，通道就成了失败的比喻。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN WAY: an alley is often a route people use to avoid the main street.
branches.cn: 暗线：小巷常是人们避开主街时走的路线。

intro.en: Alley is a French loanword with a small family built by compounding rather than suffixation.
intro.cn: alley 是法语借词，小词族靠复合构词而不是后缀派生。

latinIntro.en: The word goes back to Latin ambulare, but it entered English through French, so the Latin entries are indirect.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词上溯至拉丁语 ambulare，但经法语进入英语，因此拉丁条目是间接的。

items.example: The alley was too narrow for a car.
items.exampleCN: 这条小巷窄得车开不进去。

items.example: It is the distant source of alley.

items.exampleCN: 它的分词形式产生了 alee。

items.example: They walked through a dark alleyway.
items.exampleCN: 他们穿过一条黑暗的窄道。

items.example: An alley cat slept on the bins.
items.exampleCN: 一只流浪猫睡在垃圾桶上。

items.meaning: a place or lane for bowling
items.example: The bowling alley was full on Friday.
The route ended in a blind alley.
items.exampleCN: 这条路线终止在一条死胡同里。

definition_zh: 分配；拨给；分派；划定用途
definition_en: to give out resources, money, time, or tasks for a particular purpose
core_image: 一只手里攥着有限的筹码，逐一分到不同的格子里
scene: 校长把有限的预算分成几份，写进每个科室的表格。The council allocated more money to public transport this year.
sceneCN: 这里 allocate 是「拨给」（第 2 个义项：把资金分配给某项用途）；句意为议会今年给公共交通拨了更多钱。

pos.zh: 动词：分配；拨给；分派；划定用途

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -tion 构成，义为「分配；拨款；分配额」
由 allocation 加 -ive 构成，义为「与资源配置有关的」
由动词加 -or 构成，义为「分配者；分配程序」
由前缀 re- 加本词构成，义为「重新分配」

senses.title: To share out resources
senses.definition: to divide limited resources such as money, time, or materials among different users or purposes
senses.definitionCN: 把资金、时间或材料等有限资源分给不同使用者或用途
senses.example: The teacher allocated ten minutes to each group.
senses.exampleCN: 老师给每个小组分配了十分钟。
senses.why: Latin ad- meant to and locare meant to place; to allocate is to place each share where it belongs.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ad- 意为「向」，locare 意为「放置」；allocate 就是把每一份放到它该去的位置。

senses.title: To set money aside for a purpose
senses.definition: to reserve a sum of money officially for a particular use
senses.definitionCN: 正式为某项用途预留一笔款项
senses.example: The government allocated extra funds to rural schools.
senses.exampleCN: 政府为乡村学校拨出额外资金。
