senses.why: A budget is a grid of places, and allocating money is writing a number into one of its cells.
senses.whyCN: 预算是一张由位置组成的网格，拨款就是把一个数字写进其中一个格子里。

senses.title: To assign a task or role
senses.definition: to give a particular job or duty to a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 把某项工作或职责交给某人或某群体
senses.example: The manager allocated the most difficult cases to the senior staff.
senses.exampleCN: 经理把最难的案子分派给资深员工。
senses.why: People are also places in an organization: assigning a task is putting it into the right slot.
senses.whyCN: 人在组织中也像位置：分派任务就是把它放进合适的槽位。

intro.en: Allocate is Latin for placing something toward a purpose, and it still carries that picture of putting shares into slots.
intro.cn: allocate 在拉丁语中意为「把某物朝向某用途放置」，至今仍带着「把份额放进格子」的画面。

items.en: Latin locus meant a place, and it gives English location and local.
items.cn: 拉丁语 locus 意为地方，是英语 location 与 local 的来源。

items.en: The verb locare meant to place or set, and it is the stem behind allocate.
items.cn: 动词 locare 意为放置、安置，是 allocate 的词干来源。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant to or toward, giving the direction of the placing.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「向、朝」，给「放置」指明了方向。

items.en: Medieval Latin allocare meant to place something to a person's account or to a purpose.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 allocare 意为把某物记到某人账上或拨给某用途。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth century for official placing of money or duties.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，用于正式安排款项或职责。

items.en: Modern administration made allocate the ordinary verb of budgets and resource planning.
items.cn: 现代行政使 allocate 成为预算与资源规划中的常用动词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the allocate family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of giving out shares.
note.cn: 形近组收 allocate 词族；近义组收「分发份额」的动词。

entries.definition: The act of sharing out resources, or the share given.
entries.definitionCN: 指分配资源的行为，或分到的那一份。

entries.definition: A person or system that assigns resources.
entries.definitionCN: 指分配资源的人或系统。

entries.definition: To distribute again in a different way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以不同方式重新分配。

entries.definition: To give a task or role to a particular person.
entries.definitionCN: 指把任务或角色交给特定的人。

entries.definition: To spread or give out something among many people.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物分发给许多人。

entries.definition: To divide something into shares, often in proportion.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物按份额划分，常按比例。

entries.definition: To give a fixed share of time, money, or land.
entries.definitionCN: 指分配固定的一份时间、金钱或土地。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a hand placing counters into labelled boxes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子守住「一只手把筹码放进贴标签的盒子」这个画面。

normal.en: Allocate is ad plus locare: place each share toward its purpose.
normal.cn: allocate 是 ad 加 locare：把每一份朝它的用途放置。

normal.en: You allocate resources, time, money, or tasks, but you do not allocate feelings.
normal.cn: 你分配资源、时间、金钱或任务，但不会分配感情。

normal.en: A budget is a set of boxes, and allocating is writing numbers into them.
normal.cn: 预算就是一组盒子，拨款就是往里面写数字。

normal.en: Reallocate means the boxes were filled once and now must be rearranged.
normal.cn: reallocate 意为盒子已经装过一次，现在必须重新安排。

normal.en: Allocation can be the act or the share, so context decides which.
normal.cn: allocation 可以指行为，也可以指分到的那一份，由上下文决定。

abstract.en: Picture a handful of counters and a row of shallow trays, each with a label.
abstract.cn: 想象一把筹码和一排浅盘，每只盘子上都贴着标签。

abstract.en: The hand moves one counter at a time, never putting two where only one fits.
abstract.cn: 手一次挪一个筹码，绝不在只能放一个的地方放两个。

abstract.en: When the hand stops, the layout of counters is the allocation.
abstract.cn: 手停下时，筹码的排布就是 allocation。

examples.en: The school allocates a small budget to each club.
examples.cn: 学校给每个社团分配一小笔预算。

examples.en: We must allocate more time to the final review.
examples.cn: 我们必须给最终审查分配更多时间。

examples.en: The committee allocated the new cases to two teams.
examples.cn: 委员会把新案子分派给两个团队。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱乐凯特」——爱乐凯特把奖金一份份分给团员

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ locare（放置，源自 locus「地方」）→ 中世纪拉丁语 allocare（记到账上、拨给用途）→ 英语 allocate，核心义为「把有限的份额放置到各自的用途上」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses place resources, money, and duties into their proper slots.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项分别把资源、资金与职责放进各自合适的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holds a limited pile of counters and places them one by one into labelled trays.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手攥着有限的一堆筹码，把它们逐一放进贴好标签的盘子里。

branches.en: THE PILE: allocation begins with scarcity, because unlimited things need no sharing.
branches.cn: 筹码线：分配始于稀缺，因为无限的东西不需要分。

branches.en: THE PLACE: locare is the act of putting each share where it belongs.
branches.cn: 放置线：locare 就是把每一份放到它该在的地方。

branches.en: THE BUDGET: money is allocated by writing it into a line of an official plan.
branches.cn: 预算线：资金是通过写进正式计划的某一栏来拨出的。

branches.en: THE ROLE: people and teams are slots too, and tasks are placed into them.
branches.cn: 角色线：人和团队也是槽位，任务被放进这些槽位。

branches.en: THE RECORD: every allocation leaves a trace of who got what and why.
branches.cn: 记录线：每一次分配都留下谁得到什么、为什么得到的痕迹。

intro.en: Allocate is a Latin verb with a full derivational family and a common set of compounds for budgets and planning.
intro.cn: allocate 是拉丁语动词，有完整的派生词族，以及一套常见的预算与规划复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem locus and locare is well recorded, and the prefix ad- is equally clear.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词干 locus 与 locare 有明确记录，前缀 ad- 同样清楚。

items.meaning: to share out for a purpose
items.exampleCN: 他们每年春天分配资金。

items.example: It is the stem of allocate.
It forms allocate from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁词干构成 allocate。

items.example: The board must allocate resources fairly.
items.exampleCN: 董事会必须公平分配资源。

definition_zh: 允许；准许；使能够；承认；留出
definition_en: to let someone do something, to make something possible, or to admit a fact
core_image: 一只手把门推开一条缝，示意可以进来
scene: 考场门口，监考老师核对证件后点头放行。Visitors are not allowed to enter the laboratory without a badge.
sceneCN: 这里 allow 是「允许」（第 1 个义项：准许某人做某事）；句意为没有证件的人不允许进入实验室。

pos.zh: 动词：允许；准许；使能够；承认；留出

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可允许的；可扣除的」
由动词加 -ance 构成，义为「零花钱；津贴；限额」
由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成，义为「不准许；驳回」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「被允许的」

senses.title: To permit someone to do something
senses.definition: to give someone permission to do something or to let something happen
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人做某事的许可，或让某事发生
senses.example: My parents allow me to stay out until nine.
senses.exampleCN: 父母允许我在外面待到九点。
senses.why: The word began with a sense of approving or praising; approval became permission, the moment a door is opened for someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初有「认可、赞许」的意思；认可变成许可，就是为某人把门打开的那一刻。

senses.title: To make something possible
senses.definition: to provide the conditions or room for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 为某事发生提供条件或余地
senses.example: The extra hour allowed us to finish the experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 多出的那一小时让我们完成了实验。
senses.why: Permission and possibility share one image: something that was closed is now open enough to pass through.
senses.whyCN: 许可与可能共享同一个意象：原本关闭的东西现在开得足够让人通过。

senses.title: To admit a fact
senses.definition: to accept that something is true, often reluctantly
senses.definitionCN: 接受某事为真，常带不情愿的意味
senses.example: She allowed that the plan had one serious weakness.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认这个计划有一个严重缺陷。
senses.why: To allow a statement is to let it stand instead of pushing it away, the same opening gesture applied to an idea.
senses.whyCN: allow 一个说法，就是让它站住而不是把它推走，是把同一个「开门」动作施加到观念上。

senses.title: To set aside time or money
senses.definition: to include an amount of time or money in a plan for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 在计划中为某用途预留一定的时间或金钱
senses.example: Allow an hour for the drive to the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 去机场要留出一小时车程。
senses.why: A plan is a schedule with slots, and allowing time is opening one of those slots in advance.
senses.whyCN: 计划是一张带槽位的时间表，留出时间就是提前打开其中一个槽位。

intro.en: Allow blends two Latin verbs, one meaning to praise and one meaning to place, and the blend produced approval and permission.
intro.cn: allow 混合了两个拉丁动词，一个意为称赞，一个意为放置，这一混合产生了「认可」与「许可」。

items.en: Latin allaudare meant to praise or approve, built from ad- plus laudare, to praise.
items.cn: 拉丁语 allaudare 意为称赞或认可，由 ad- 加 laudare（称赞）构成。

items.en: Latin allocare meant to place or assign, built from ad- plus locare, to place.
items.cn: 拉丁语 allocare 意为放置或分配，由 ad- 加 locare（放置）构成。

items.en: Old French alouer blended the two Latin verbs, carrying both approval and allocation into one word.
items.cn: 古法语 alouer 把两个拉丁动词混在一起，让「认可」与「分配」进入同一个词。

items.en: Middle English allowen first meant to approve or commend something as good.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 allowen 最初意为认可或称赞某物为好。

items.en: From approval came the sense of granting permission and letting something happen.
items.cn: 从「认可」生出授予许可、让某事发生的义项。

items.en: The sense of admitting a fact grew later, when a statement is allowed to stand.
items.cn: 「承认事实」的义项出现较晚，指让一个说法站得住。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the allow family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of permission and enabling.
note.cn: 形近组收 allow 词族；近义组收表示许可与使能的动词。

entries.definition: Permitted by rules, especially for costs or claims.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则允许的，尤用于费用或索赔。

entries.definition: A sum of money or a permitted amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指一笔钱或允许的数量。

entries.definition: To refuse to accept or permit.
entries.definitionCN: 指拒绝接受或准许。

entries.definition: Permitted, or the past form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指被允许的，或该动词的过去形式。

entries.definition: To give official or formal permission.
entries.definitionCN: 指给予正式或官方的许可。

entries.definition: To allow something without resistance, the plainest verb of the group.
entries.definitionCN: 指不加阻拦地允许，是本组最朴素的动词。

entries.definition: To give official power or approval for an action.
entries.definitionCN: 指为某项行动授予正式权力或批准。

entries.definition: To make something possible by providing the means.
entries.definitionCN: 指提供手段使某事成为可能。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the door from praise to permission and then to possibility.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子跟着那扇门，从赞许走到许可，再走到可能。

normal.en: Allow began as approval, so permission is approval put into action.
normal.cn: allow 原先是认可，所以许可是被付诸行动的认可。

normal.en: Be allowed to is the passive pattern; allow someone to is the active one.
normal.cn: be allowed to 是被动句式；allow someone to 是主动句式。

normal.en: Allow for means leave room for, the same opening gesture in a plan.
normal.cn: allow for 意为留出余地，是同一个开门动作用在计划里。

normal.en: Allow that is to let a fact stand, even if you do not like it.
normal.cn: allow that 是让一个事实站住，即使你不喜欢它。

normal.en: Disallow is the closed door: the same verb with a negative prefix.
normal.cn: disallow 是关上的门：同一个动词加上否定前缀。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy door opened just wide enough for one person to slip through.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇沉重的门只开到刚好够一个人侧身过去的宽度。

abstract.en: The gap is permission; the person passing through is the action that follows.
abstract.cn: 这道缝是许可；穿过去的人是随后发生的行动。

abstract.en: Widen the gap for a whole group and allow becomes a general condition.
abstract.cn: 把缝开大到够一群人通过，allow 就变成一种普遍条件。

examples.en: The rules do not allow food in the library.
examples.cn: 规定不允许把食物带进图书馆。

examples.en: Allow twenty minutes for the walk to the station.
examples.cn: 去车站走路要留出二十分钟。

examples.en: He allowed that the delay was partly his fault.
examples.cn: 他承认延误部分是他的错。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额老」——额，老师点头，准许你进教室

root: 古法语 alouer 混合了两个拉丁动词：allaudare（称赞、认可）与 allocare（放置、分配）；由「认可」生出「准许」，再由「准许」生出「使可能、承认、留出」。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses all describe an opening: permission, possibility, admission, and reserved room.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都在描述一种「打开」：许可、可能、承认，以及预留的余地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushes a door open just far enough, and the gap says yes without a word.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把门推到刚好够开的程度，这道缝不用说话就表示了同意。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: the oldest sense is approval, and permission is approval made practical.
branches.cn: 赞许线：最古老的义项是认可，许可是被实用化的认可。

branches.en: THE GAP: opening the door is the physical form of saying yes.
branches.cn: 门缝线：把门打开就是说「可以」的身体形式。

branches.en: THE PASSAGE: once the door is open, what follows can actually happen.
branches.cn: 通过线：门一开，随后的事情才能真正发生。

branches.en: THE STATEMENT: an idea is also let through when a fact is admitted.
branches.cn: 说法线：承认一个事实时，一个观念也被放行了。

branches.en: THE SLOT: in a plan, the open door becomes a reserved block of time or money.
branches.cn: 槽位线：在计划里，打开的门变成预留的一段时间或一笔钱。

intro.en: Allow has a compact but common suffix family, and its compounds are fixed verb phrases rather than nouns.
intro.cn: allow 有紧凑而常用的后缀词族，它的复合形式是固定动词短语而不是名词。

latinIntro.en: Two Latin verbs stand behind the word, and both are recorded clearly enough to list.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后有两个拉丁动词，记录都足够清楚，可以列出。

items.example: They allow pets in the hotel.
It is one source of allow.
items.exampleCN: 它是 allow 的来源之一。

items.example: It is the other source of allow.
items.exampleCN: 它是 allow 的另一个来源。

items.example: Allow for traffic on the way.
items.exampleCN: 路上要考虑到交通状况。

items.example: The badge allows access to the lab.
items.exampleCN: 这张证件允许进入实验室。

definition_zh: 零花钱；津贴；限额；体谅
definition_en: a regular sum of money given to someone, an official limit, or the act of allowing
core_image: 每周固定放在孩子手里的一小叠零钱
scene: 父亲每月把一笔钱放进孩子的账户，让他自己学着花。Her parents give her a small allowance for school supplies.
sceneCN: 这里 allowance 是「零花钱」（第 1 个义项：定期给孩子的钱）；句意为她父母给她一小笔买学习用品的零花钱。

pos.zh: 名词：零花钱；津贴；限额；体谅

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀得到的基础动词，义为「允许；留出」
由 allow 加 -able 构成，义为「可允许的；可扣除的」
由否定前缀 dis- 加 allow 构成，义为「不准许」

senses.title: Regular pocket money
senses.definition: a small regular sum of money given to a child or dependent person
senses.definitionCN: 定期给儿童或受抚养人的一小笔钱
senses.example: He saves half of his weekly allowance.
senses.exampleCN: 他把每周零花钱的一半存起来。
senses.why: An allowance is an amount allowed: money handed over on the understanding that it is yours to use.
senses.whyCN: allowance 是一笔「被允许」的数额：交到你手上，并默认由你支配。

senses.title: An official payment
senses.definition: a sum paid regularly for a particular purpose, such as travel or housing
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途定期支付的款项，如差旅或住房补贴
senses.example: The job comes with a housing allowance.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作附带住房津贴。
senses.why: The same permitted sum becomes an institutional payment, with a purpose attached to it.
senses.whyCN: 同一笔被允许的数额变成机构支付，并附上特定用途。

senses.title: A permitted limit
senses.definition: an amount of something that rules permit, such as luggage weight or tax-free income
senses.definitionCN: 规则允许的数量，如行李重量或免税收入额
senses.example: Each passenger has a baggage allowance of twenty kilos.
senses.exampleCN: 每位乘客的行李限额是二十公斤。
senses.why: Here the word measures permission rather than money: the limit is how much you are allowed.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词衡量的是许可而不是金钱：限额就是你被允许的数量。

senses.title: Considerate allowance for difficulties
senses.definition: the act of taking someone's difficulty into account, as in make allowance for
senses.definitionCN: 把某人的困难纳入考虑的行为，用于 make allowance for
senses.example: We must make allowance for her lack of experience.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须体谅她经验不足。
senses.why: To make allowance for something is to leave a permitted margin around it, the same idea applied to human weakness.
senses.whyCN: make allowance for 某事物，就是在它周围留出被允许的余量，同一个观念用在人的弱点上。

intro.en: Allowance is allow plus the noun suffix -ance, and its money sense came later than its sense of permission.
intro.cn: allowance 是 allow 加名词后缀 -ance，它表示金钱的义项晚于表示许可的义项。

items.en: The base verb came from Old French alouer, meaning to approve or grant.
items.cn: 基础动词来自古法语 alouer，意为认可或授予。

items.en: The suffix -ance, from Latin -antia, turns a verb into a noun of action or amount.
items.cn: 后缀 -ance 来自拉丁语 -antia，把动词变成表示行为或数量的名词。

items.en: Allowance first meant approval or permission, the act of allowing something.
items.cn: allowance 最初意为认可或许可，即允许某事的行为。

items.en: The sense of a regular sum given to a dependent person developed in modern household usage.
items.cn: 定期给受抚养人的一笔钱这一义项，在现代家庭用语中发展出来。

items.en: Trade and transport rules gave the word the sense of a permitted quantity.
items.cn: 贸易与运输规则给这个词添了「被允许数量」的义项。

items.en: The phrase make allowance for extended the permitted margin to human understanding.
items.cn: 短语 make allowance for 把被允许的余量延伸到人的体谅。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the allow family; the near-meaning group gathers sums, limits and grants.
note.cn: 形近组收 allow 词族；近义组收款项、限额与补助。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to permit or set aside.
entries.definitionCN: 指允许或留出的动词。

entries.definition: Permitted by rules, especially for expenses.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则允许的，尤用于开支。

entries.definition: To refuse to permit or accept.
entries.definitionCN: 指拒绝允许或接受。

entries.definition: Small regular money for a child's personal spending.
entries.definitionCN: 指给孩子个人花销的少量定期钱款。

entries.definition: A fixed regular payment, especially to a student or clergy member.
entries.definitionCN: 指固定定期支付，尤给学生或神职人员。

entries.definition: A fixed share or maximum number that is allowed.
entries.definitionCN: 指被允许的固定份额或最大数量。

entries.definition: Money paid by a system to support someone.
entries.definitionCN: 指由制度支付以支持某人的钱。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the permitted amount at the centre while the purpose changes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把「被允许的数额」放在中心，只让用途变化。

normal.en: Allowance is allow plus -ance: the amount that has been allowed to you.
normal.cn: allowance 是 allow 加 -ance：已经被允许给你的那笔数额。

normal.en: A child's allowance is money; an airline allowance is weight; a tax allowance is income.
normal.cn: 孩子的 allowance 是钱；航空公司的 allowance 是重量；免税 allowance 是收入。

normal.en: Make allowance for means leave a margin for human difficulty.
normal.cn: make allowance for 意为为人的困难留出余量。

normal.en: Baggage allowance is a permission measured in kilos.
normal.cn: baggage allowance 是以公斤计量的许可。

normal.en: Monthly allowance is the same sum arriving on a schedule.
normal.cn: monthly allowance 是同一笔钱按时间表到来。

abstract.en: Picture a small stack of coins placed on a table every Sunday morning.
abstract.cn: 想象每个星期天早上，桌上都会放下一小叠硬币。

abstract.en: The stack is not a gift and not a wage: it is an amount measured out in advance.
abstract.cn: 这叠硬币既不是礼物也不是工资：它是提前量好的一份数额。

abstract.en: Change the unit from coins to kilos and the same idea becomes a baggage allowance.
abstract.cn: 把单位从硬币换成公斤，同一个观念就成了行李限额。

examples.en: She spends her allowance on bus fares and books.
examples.cn: 她把零花钱花在车费和书上。

examples.en: The airline raised its baggage allowance to twenty-five kilos.
examples.cn: 航空公司把行李限额提高到二十五公斤。

examples.en: Please make allowance for the fact that he is new to the job.
examples.cn: 请体谅他刚做这份工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额老恩斯」——额，老师恩斯给的零花钱

root: allow（允许，源自古法语 alouer，混合拉丁语 allaudare「称赞」与 allocare「放置、分配」）加名词后缀 -ance（行为或数量）；核心为「被允许的一份数额」。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses are one permitted amount measured in money, in payment, in quantity, and in understanding.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项是同一笔「被允许的数额」，分别用金钱、支付、数量与体谅来衡量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small measured portion is set on the table in advance, and it belongs to the person who receives it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小份量好的东西被提前放在桌上，归收下它的人支配。

branches.en: THE COINS: the household sense is a regular small sum for personal use.
branches.cn: 硬币线：家庭义项是供个人使用的定期小额钱款。

branches.en: THE PAYMENT: institutions pay the same kind of measured sum for a purpose.
branches.cn: 支付线：机构为特定用途支付同一种量好的数额。

branches.en: THE LIMIT: the amount can be measured in kilos or tax-free income instead of coins.
branches.cn: 限额线：这份数额可以用公斤或免税收入来衡量，而不只是硬币。

branches.en: THE MARGIN: understanding gives a person the same kind of permitted room.
branches.cn: 余量线：体谅给人的正是同一种被允许的余地。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: in every sense something has been measured out before it is given.
branches.cn: 量度线：无论哪个义项，东西在给出之前都已被量好。

intro.en: Allowance is a suffix noun on allow, and its compounds name the purpose of the permitted sum.
intro.cn: allowance 是在 allow 上加后缀构成的名词，复合词则命名这笔被允许款项的用途。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -ance and the base verb both have clear Latin origins, though the verb arrived through French.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -ance 与基础动词都有清楚的拉丁来源，不过动词是经法语传来的。

items.example: The allowance covers books and transport.
items.exampleCN: 这笔零花钱涵盖书本和交通。

items.example: They allow two hours for lunch.
items.exampleCN: 他们留出两小时吃午饭。

items.example: Check your baggage allowance before flying.
The tax allowance rose this year.

definition_zh: 几乎；差不多；将近
definition_en: very nearly, but not completely
core_image: 一支箭擦着靶心飞过，只差一点点
scene: 终点线就在眼前，他却在这时绊了一下。She almost missed the last train home.
sceneCN: 这里 almost 是「差一点」（第 3 个义项：几乎要发生而未发生）；句意为她差一点错过了最后一班回家的火车。

pos.zh: 副词：几乎；差不多；将近

derivatives.zh: 与 almost 共享 most 词干，义为「最多的；大多数的」
由 most 加 -ly 构成，义为「主要地；多半」
由古英语词素构成，与 most 同源，义为「极度的；最大的」

senses.title: Very nearly, in degree
senses.definition: used with an adjective or verb to mean to a very great degree but not fully
senses.definitionCN: 与形容词或动词连用，表示程度极深但未完全达到
senses.example: The room was almost dark when we arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 我们到的时候，房间几乎全黑了。
senses.why: All plus most meant the greatest part; almost is that whole reduced by one small step, so the degree stops just short of complete.
senses.whyCN: all 加 most 原意为「最大的部分」；almost 就是那个整体退后一小步，所以程度在「完全」之前停住。

senses.title: Nearly, in number or time
senses.definition: used with numbers, amounts, or periods to mean slightly less than the stated figure
senses.definitionCN: 与数字、数量或时段连用，表示略少于所说的数值
senses.example: Almost forty students signed up for the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 将近四十名学生报名参加了这次旅行。
senses.why: The same small gap appears on a scale: the count is not complete, but it has reached the neighbourhood of the figure.
senses.whyCN: 同一个小缺口出现在刻度上：数目没有到齐，却已经接近那个数值。

senses.title: Just short of happening
senses.titleCN: 差一点（几乎发生而未发生）
senses.definition: used to say that something nearly happened but did not
senses.definitionCN: 用来说某事几乎发生，但最终没有发生
senses.example: He almost fell asleep during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座期间他差点睡着了。
senses.why: Here the gap is an event: the arrow passes the target by a hair, and the miss is the point of the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 这里的缺口是一个事件：箭擦着靶心飞过，而「没中」正是这句话的重点。

intro.en: Almost is a fused Old English phrase meaning all most, and the small gap between all and most became its meaning.
intro.cn: almost 是古英语短语「all most」融合而成，all 与 most 之间那一小段距离成了它的词义。

items.en: Eall meant all or whole, the first half of the phrase.
items.cn: eall 意为全部、整体，是短语的前半部分。

items.en: Mǣst meant most or greatest, the second half of the phrase.
items.cn: mǣst 意为最多、最大，是短语的后半部分。

items.en: The two words were spoken together so often that they fused into a single adverb.
items.cn: 两个词经常连说，最终融合成一个副词。

items.en: Middle English almost kept the sense of nearly all, then widened to nearly in general.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 almost 保留「几乎全部」的意思，后扩展到泛指「几乎」。

items.en: The word attached to adjectives and verbs, becoming a general marker of near completion.
items.cn: 这个词开始附着在形容词与动词上，成为「接近完成」的通用标记。

items.en: Almost now covers degree, number, and near events, always keeping the same small gap.
items.cn: 现代 almost 覆盖程度、数量与险些发生的事件，始终保留同一个小缺口。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same most stem; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of near completion.
note.cn: 形近组收来自同一 most 词干的词；近义组收表示接近完成的副词。

entries.definition: The greatest amount, or the majority of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指最大数量，或一个群体中的大多数。

entries.definition: Mainly or usually, not completely.
entries.definitionCN: 指主要地或通常，并非完全。

entries.definition: The greatest possible degree of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指某事物可能达到的最大程度。

entries.definition: Very close to a state or amount, often interchangeable with almost.
entries.definitionCN: 指非常接近某状态或数量，常可与 almost 互换。

entries.definition: In effect or very nearly, used in informal speech.
entries.definitionCN: 指实际上或几乎，多用于口语。

entries.definition: Almost entirely, often before an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指几乎完全地，常放在形容词前。

entries.definition: Approximately, used with numbers rather than with events.
entries.definitionCN: 指大约，多与数字连用而不是与事件连用。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the tiny gap between all and most in view.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子始终盯着 all 与 most 之间那个小缺口。

normal.en: Almost is all most: everything except a little bit.
normal.cn: almost 是 all most：除了那么一点点，其他全都有了。

normal.en: Use almost with adjectives and verbs; use most with nouns to mean the majority.
normal.cn: almost 配形容词和动词；most 配名词表示大多数。

normal.en: Almost never and almost always are the two ends of the same scale.
normal.cn: almost never 与 almost always 是同一刻度上的两端。

normal.en: Almost missed the train means the train was caught, but only just.
normal.cn: almost missed the train 意为赶上了火车，只是差一点没赶上。

normal.en: Almost impossible still leaves a narrow chance open.
normal.cn: almost impossible 仍留着一线狭窄的机会。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow passing so close to the centre that it cuts one hair from the target.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭贴着靶心飞过，只削掉靶上的一根细线。

abstract.en: The arrow is gone, the target is almost hit, and the gap is the whole story.
abstract.cn: 箭已经飞过，靶几乎被命中，而那道缝隙就是整个故事。

abstract.en: Put the same gap on a clock or a crowd and almost measures time and number too.
abstract.cn: 把同一道缝隙放到钟表或人群上，almost 也衡量时间与数量。

examples.en: It is almost midnight, and the shop is still open.
examples.cn: 已经将近午夜，商店还开着。

examples.en: She almost dropped the glass when the phone rang.
examples.cn: 电话响时她差点把杯子掉了。

examples.en: Almost everyone in the village came to the wedding.
examples.cn: 村里几乎所有人都来参加婚礼了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶么事都」——偶么事都做完了，几乎全做完

root: 古英语短语 eall（全部）+ mǣst（最多）融合而成，字面为「几乎全部」；后扩展为程度、数量上的「将近」，以及事件上的「差一点」。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses put the same small gap on a degree, a number, and an event.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项把同一个小缺口分别放在程度、数量与事件上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow passes the target by the width of a hair, close enough to touch but not to hit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支箭以一根头发丝的宽度擦过靶心，近得能碰到，却没有命中。

branches.en: THE DEGREE: the gap sits between nearly and completely on an adjective.
branches.cn: 程度线：缺口停在形容词上「几乎」与「完全」之间。

branches.en: THE SCALE: the same gap appears just below a stated number or hour.
branches.cn: 刻度线：同一个缺口出现在所说数字或钟点的下方一点。

branches.en: THE EVENT: when the gap is a moment, the sentence is about what nearly happened.
branches.cn: 事件线：当缺口是一个瞬间，句子讲的就是险些发生的事。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: all and most remain visible inside the word, so the idea of a complete set never disappears.
branches.cn: 整体线：all 与 most 仍留在词里，所以「完整集合」的观念从未消失。

branches.en: THE RELIEF: almost missed carries relief, because the miss did not happen.
branches.cn: 庆幸线：almost missed 带着庆幸，因为「没赶上」并没有发生。

intro.en: Almost is a fused native phrase, so its family comes from the shared most stem rather than from suffixes on almost itself.
intro.cn: almost 是本土短语融合词，它的词族来自共享的 most 词干，而不是加在 almost 本身的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is entirely Old English, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词完全属于古英语，因此拉丁条目为空。

items.example: It is the first half of almost.
items.exampleCN: 它是 almost 的前半部分。

items.example: It is the second half of almost.
items.exampleCN: 它是 almost 的后半部分。

items.example: They treated us with the utmost care.
items.exampleCN: 他们以最大的细心对待我们。

items.example: Almost all the seats were sold.
items.exampleCN: 几乎所有座位都卖掉了。

definition_zh: 独自的；单独的；仅仅；孤独的
definition_en: without other people; only; or feeling isolated
core_image: 一间亮着灯的屋子，桌边只坐了一个人
scene: 整栋楼都熄了灯，只有她的窗户还亮着。He lives alone in a small flat near the station.
sceneCN: 这里 alone 是「独自」（第 1 个义项：没有他人陪伴）；句意为他独自住在车站附近的一间小公寓里。

pos.zh: 形容词：独自的；单独的；孤独的（多作表语）
副词：独自地；单独地；仅仅

derivatives.zh: 由 alone 去掉前缀 a- 而来，义为「单独的；孤单的」
由 lone 加 -ly 构成，义为「孤独的；寂寞的」
由 lonely 加 -ness 构成，义为「孤独；寂寞」
由 lone 加 -some 构成，义为「孤寂的；荒凉的」

senses.title: Without other people
senses.definition: being the only person present, with no one else there
senses.definitionCN: 指在场只有自己一个人，没有他人在旁
senses.example: She sat alone at the back of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 她独自坐在大厅后排。
senses.why: Alone began as all one, meaning a single person or thing by itself; the many have become one.
senses.whyCN: alone 最初是 all one，意为单独一个人或一件物；众多变成了一。

senses.title: Only, and nothing more
senses.definition: used after a noun to mean and nothing or no one else, as in money alone
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词之后，表示「仅仅、再无其他」，如 money alone
senses.example: The name alone tells you how famous he is.
senses.exampleCN: 单是这个名字就能说明他有多有名。
senses.why: The all-one picture turns into emphasis: one element stands by itself and excludes every other.
senses.whyCN: 「全部成为一」的画面转成强调：一个要素独立站着，把其余一切都排除在外。

senses.title: By one's own effort
senses.definition: without help from others, doing something by oneself
senses.definitionCN: 没有他人帮助，靠自己完成某事
senses.example: He built the whole shed alone.
senses.exampleCN: 他一个人搭起了整间棚屋。
senses.why: This is the adverb at work: the single person is not merely present but is the only agent.
senses.whyCN: 这是副词用法：这一个人不仅在场，而且是唯一的行动者。

senses.title: Feeling isolated
senses.definition: feeling unhappy because of a lack of company, even if others are nearby
senses.definitionCN: 因缺少陪伴而感到不快，即使附近有别人
senses.example: He felt alone even in the crowded room.
senses.exampleCN: 即使在拥挤的房间里，他仍感到孤独。
senses.why: Physical solitude becomes an emotional state: being one among many can still feel like being the only one.
senses.whyCN: 身体上的独处变成情感状态：身处众人之中，仍可能觉得只有自己。

intro.en: Alone is all one written as a single word, and the road from all one to lonely passes through a change of feeling.
intro.cn: alone 是 all one 写成一个词；从「全部成为一」走到「孤独」，中间经历了一次感受的转变。

items.en: The phrase all ān meant all one or one only, a single person or thing by itself.
items.cn: 短语 all ān 意为「全是一」或「只有一个」，指独自一人或一物。

items.en: The two words fused into alone, and the first syllable weakened to a-.
items.cn: 两个词融合成 alone，第一个音节弱化为 a-。

items.en: Because it names a state, alone stayed after the verb rather than before a noun.
items.cn: 因为它命名状态，alone 留在动词之后，而不放在名词之前。

items.en: The sense of one by itself produced the emphatic use after nouns, as in the name alone.
items.cn: 「独自一个」的含义生出名词后的强调用法，如 the name alone。

items.en: By the modern period alone could describe unhappy isolation, not only physical solitude.
items.cn: 到现代时期，alone 已能描述不快的情感孤立，而不只是身体独处。

items.en: English built lone, lonely, loneliness and lonesome from the same single-self idea.
items.cn: 英语由同一个「独一自我」的观念造出 lone、lonely、loneliness 与 lonesome。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the lone family; the near-meaning group gathers words for solitude and being unaccompanied.
note.cn: 形近组收 lone 词族；近义组收表示独处与无人陪伴的词。

entries.definition: Single or solitary, often used before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个的或孤独的，常放在名词前。

entries.definition: Feeling sad because of a lack of company.
entries.definitionCN: 指因缺少陪伴而感到悲伤。

entries.definition: The state of feeling lonely.
entries.definitionCN: 指感到孤独的状态。

entries.definition: A warmer or more literary word for lonely and remote.
entries.definitionCN: 指孤独而偏僻的，语气更温暖或更文学化。

entries.definition: Done alone or living alone, often by choice.
entries.definitionCN: 指独自做的或独自生活的，常出于自愿。

entries.definition: One and not more than one, without the emotional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个而非更多，不带情感含义。

entries.definition: Going somewhere without a companion.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有同伴而前往某处。

entries.definition: Cut off from others, often by distance or circumstances.
entries.definitionCN: 指因距离或环境而与他人隔绝。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with all one and split it into presence, emphasis, effort, and feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从 all one 出发，把它分成在场、强调、努力与感受四个方面。

normal.en: Alone is all one: a group of one.
normal.cn: alone 是 all one：只有一个人的一群。

normal.en: Live alone is neutral; feel alone is sad; the grammar is the same, the feeling is not.
normal.cn: live alone 是中性的；feel alone 是悲伤的；语法相同，感受不同。

normal.en: Let alone means not to mention, because the first case already stands by itself.
normal.cn: let alone 意为更不用说，因为第一种情况已经独自成立。

normal.en: Leave me alone is a request for space, not a statement that you are lonely.
normal.cn: leave me alone 是请求空间，而不是声明你孤独。

normal.en: Go it alone means act without partners, the single self as the only agent.
normal.cn: go it alone 意为没有伙伴独自行动，把独一自我当作唯一行动者。

abstract.en: Picture a lit window in a dark building, and one chair pulled up to one table.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗楼里一扇亮着的窗，一张桌子旁只拉出一把椅子。

abstract.en: The light does not say whether the person is content or sad; only the context does.
abstract.cn: 灯光并不说明这个人是满足还是悲伤，只有上下文才知道。

abstract.en: Alone keeps that double door open: solitude and loneliness share one word.
abstract.cn: alone 让那扇双开门保持敞开：独处与孤独共用同一个词。

examples.en: She prefers to work alone in the early morning.
examples.cn: 她更喜欢在清早独自工作。

examples.en: The house stood alone at the end of the lane.
examples.cn: 那栋房子孤零零地立在巷子尽头。

examples.en: You cannot live on bread alone.
examples.cn: 单靠面包无法生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额龙」——额，一条龙独自盘在空屋里

root: 古英语短语 all ān（全是一、只有一个）融合而成，第一个音节弱化为 a-；由「独自一个」引申出「仅仅」，再引申出「孤独」的情感义。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses move from physical solitude to emphasis, to independent effort, and finally to emotional isolation.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项从身体独处，走到强调、独立完成，最后落到情感上的孤立。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lit window in a dark building, and one chair at one table.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗楼里只有一扇亮窗，一张桌子旁只有一把椅子。

branches.en: THE SINGLE: the oldest sense is a group reduced to one person.
branches.cn: 独一线：最古老的义项是一个群体缩减到一个人。

branches.en: THE ONLY: one element stands alone and excludes everything else.
branches.cn: 唯一线：一个要素独自站着，把其余一切都排除。

branches.en: THE EFFORT: the single person is not only present but is the sole worker.
branches.cn: 努力线：这一个人不仅在场，还是唯一的劳动者。

branches.en: THE FEELING: physical solitude can turn into emotional isolation.
branches.cn: 感受线：身体的独处可以转成情感的孤立。

branches.en: THE INDEPENDENCE: the same word can praise self-reliance or pity loneliness.
branches.cn: 独立线：同一个词既能称赞自立，也能怜悯孤独。

intro.en: Alone is a fused native phrase, and its family grew from the stripped stem lone plus ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: alone 是本土短语融合词，它的词族由去掉前缀的词干 lone 加普通后缀长出。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Old English, so there are no Latin entries.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于本土古英语，因此没有拉丁条目。

items.example: He was alone in the house.
It is the first half of alone.
items.exampleCN: 它是 alone 的前半部分。

items.example: It is the second half of alone.
items.exampleCN: 它是 alone 的后半部分。

items.example: A lone tree stood on the hill.
He cannot walk, let alone run.
items.exampleCN: 他走都走不了，更不用说跑。

definition_zh: 沿着；顺着；向前；一起
definition_en: from one end of something towards the other, forward, or together with someone
core_image: 一条路伸向远方，脚步贴着路边一直向前
scene: 他们沿着河岸慢慢走，脚下的石子被水冲得发亮。We walked along the river until the sun went down.
sceneCN: 这里 along 是「沿着」（第 1 个义项：从一端向另一端顺着走）；句意为我们沿着河一直走到太阳落山。

pos.zh: 介词：沿着；顺着；在……期间
副词：向前；一起；来到

derivatives.zh: 由 along 与 side 构成的复合词，义为「在……旁边」
由 along 与 shore 构成的复合词，义为「沿岸地」
固定短语，义为「与……一起」

senses.title: Following the length of something
senses.definition: from one end of a line, road, or surface towards the other, staying close to it
senses.definitionCN: 从一条线、道路或表面的一端向另一端，贴着它移动
senses.example: We cycled along the canal for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 我们沿着运河骑了两个小时。
senses.why: Old English andlang meant entirely long, built from and- plus lang, long; to go along is to follow the full length of something.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 andlang 意为「整个地长」，由 and- 加 lang（长）构成；go along 就是顺着某物的整个长度走。

senses.title: Forward or onward
senses.definition: moving forward or continuing on a course
senses.definitionCN: 向前移动，或沿某条路线继续
senses.example: The train moved along slowly through the fog.
senses.exampleCN: 火车在雾中缓慢向前行驶。
senses.why: If the line is long, moving along it is moving forward; the word carries both the line and the motion.
senses.whyCN: 如果线是长的，沿着它移动就是向前；这个词同时带着线与运动。

senses.title: Together with someone
senses.definition: in company with another person, often in phrases such as come along or bring along
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人同行，常用于 come along 或 bring along 等短语
senses.example: Why not bring your sister along?
senses.exampleCN: 为什么不带你妹妹一起来？
senses.why: Two people walking the same line are side by side; companionship is the same picture with a second traveller.
senses.whyCN: 两个人走同一条线就是并肩；陪伴只是同一画面里多了一个同行者。

intro.en: Along began as a word for the full length of something, and then split into a line, a direction, and a companion.
intro.cn: along 最初指某物的整个长度，后来分成一条线、一个方向与一位同行者。

items.en: Old English andlang meant along or entirely, built from and- plus lang, long.
items.cn: 古英语 andlang 意为沿着或完全地，由 and- 加 lang（长）构成。

items.en: The prefix and- meant through or throughout, giving the sense of covering a whole extent.
items.cn: 前缀 and- 意为穿过、贯穿，带来「覆盖整个范围」的含义。

items.en: Lang meant long, so the word pictured a long line being followed from end to end.
items.cn: lang 意为长，所以这个词描绘一条长线被从头到尾跟随。

items.en: The form along settled, and the word worked as both preposition and adverb.
items.cn: along 的形式固定下来，同时作介词与副词。

items.en: Motion along a line became simple onward movement, as in move along.
items.cn: 沿线的运动变成单纯的向前移动，如 move along。

items.en: Come along and bring along added a second traveller to the same line.
items.cn: come along 与 bring along 在同一条线上添了第二位同行者。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers along compounds; the near-meaning group gathers words for position and direction.
note.cn: 形近组收 along 的复合词；近义组收表示位置与方向的词。

entries.definition: Next to the side of something, or together with it.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某物旁边，或与它一起。

entries.definition: Along the shore or coast.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿岸地；沿着海岸。

entries.definition: The adjective of length behind the second half of along.
entries.definitionCN: 指长度形容词，是 along 后半部分的来源。

entries.definition: At the side of someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某人或某物旁边。

entries.definition: Towards the front or towards a later point.
entries.definitionCN: 指朝前方或朝更后的位置。

entries.definition: In the direction of the length of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿某物长度的方向。

entries.definition: With each other, in one group or at one time.
entries.definitionCN: 指彼此在一起，在同一群或同一时间。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the long line and attach direction and company to it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子守住那条长线，并把方向与陪伴挂上去。

normal.en: Along came from all-long: follow the whole length of the line.
normal.cn: along 来自「整个长度」：顺着这条线的全部长度走。

normal.en: Walk along the river means keep the river beside you.
normal.cn: walk along the river 意为让河一直陪在你旁边。

normal.en: Move along is a pure direction phrase: no object, just forward.
normal.cn: move along 是纯方向短语：没有宾语，只是向前。

normal.en: Come along adds a person to the same line you are walking.
normal.cn: come along 把一个人加到你所走的同一条线上。

normal.en: Along with means in company with, and get along means travel well together.
normal.cn: along with 意为与……一道；get along 意为相处得好。

abstract.en: Picture a long rope laid on the ground from one post to another.
abstract.cn: 想象一根长绳铺在地上，从一个木桩延伸到另一个木桩。

abstract.en: Your feet stay beside the rope as you walk its full length.
abstract.cn: 你走完整根绳时，双脚一直贴着它。

abstract.en: Add a second walker beside you, and the same rope explains come along.
abstract.cn: 在你身旁再加一个走者，同一根绳就解释了 come along。

examples.en: They planted trees along both sides of the road.
examples.cn: 他们在道路两旁种了树。

examples.en: We sang songs along the way to the campsite.
examples.cn: 去营地的路上我们一路唱歌。

examples.en: Bring your notebook along to the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会时把你的笔记本带上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额龙」——额，一条龙沿着河岸向前游

root: 古英语 andlang（整个长度地），由 and-（贯穿）加 lang（长）构成；本义为顺着某物的全长移动，后引申为向前、一起。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses take one long line and turn it into a route, a direction, and a shared journey.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项把同一条长线，分别变成路线、方向与共同旅程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long rope lies from one post to another, and a pair of feet follows it without leaving its side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根长绳从一个木桩铺到另一个木桩，一双脚贴着它一路跟随。

branches.en: THE ROPE: the first sense follows the full length of a thing.
branches.cn: 绳索线：第一个义项顺着某物的整个长度。

branches.en: THE DIRECTION: once you follow the line, you are moving forward.
branches.cn: 方向线：一旦顺着线走，你就在向前移动。

branches.en: THE COMPANION: a second walker on the same line turns direction into company.
branches.cn: 同伴线：同一条线上的第二个走者，把方向变成陪伴。

branches.en: THE SHARED PATH: along with and get along both keep two parties on one route.
branches.cn: 共路字线：along with 与 get along 都让两方处在同一条路线上。

branches.en: THE PROGRESS: moving along can mean continuing a project, not only walking.
branches.cn: 进展线：moving along 可以指继续推进项目，而不只是走路。

intro.en: Along is a native word that mostly builds compounds, and its second element long is still visible in the spelling.
intro.cn: along 是本土词，主要靠复合构词，它的第二成分 long 仍能在拼写中看见。

latinIntro.en: The word is Old English, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于古英语，因此拉丁条目为空。

items.example: It is the second half of andlang.
items.exampleCN: 它是 andlang 的后半部分。

items.example: She came along with her friend.
The two brothers get along well.

definition_zh: 在……旁边；与……并肩；与……同时；与……相比
definition_en: next to the side of something, together with someone, or at the same time as something
core_image: 两条船并排停靠，船舷贴着船舷
scene: 拖船靠上大船，两艘船并排缓缓驶出港口。A small boat moved alongside the ship to deliver supplies.
sceneCN: 这里 alongside 是「在……旁边」（第 1 个义项：紧靠某物的侧面）；句意为一只小船靠到大船旁边运送补给。

pos.zh: 介词：在……旁边；与……一起；与……相比
副词：并排地；靠边地

derivatives.zh: 同源词，alongside 的第一成分，义为「沿着」
同源词，alongside 的第二成分，义为「侧面、旁边」
同义近形词，义为「在……旁边」

senses.title: Next to the side of something
senses.definition: positioned next to the side of a ship, road, building, or other object
senses.definitionCN: 位于船、道路、建筑或其他物体的侧面旁边
senses.example: The car parked alongside the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车停在栅栏旁边。
senses.why: Along plus side is almost a definition: moving along the side of a thing places you right next to it.
senses.whyCN: along 加 side 几乎就是定义：顺着某物的侧面移动，就把你放在它旁边。

senses.title: Side by side
senses.definition: used as an adverb for two things positioned side by side
senses.definitionCN: 作副词，表示两个事物并排停靠或放置
senses.example: The two boats floated alongside in the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 两艘船在港里并排漂着。
senses.why: The noun side becomes a position: both objects keep one flank turned toward the other.
senses.whyCN: 名词 side 变成一种位置：两个物体各把一个侧面朝向对方。

senses.title: Working together with someone
senses.definition: in cooperation with another person or group, often in work or struggle
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人或群体合作，常用于工作或斗争语境
senses.example: She worked alongside doctors in the field hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 她在野战医院与医生们并肩工作。
senses.why: Two people at the same side of a task are side by side, and cooperation is that shared flank in action.
senses.whyCN: 两个人处在任务的同一侧就是并肩，合作就是那个共同侧面在行动。

senses.title: At the same time, or compared with
senses.definition: existing at the same time as something else, or considered next to it for comparison
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物同时存在，或被放在它旁边作比较
senses.example: Alongside these gains, the report notes rising costs.
senses.exampleCN: 在取得这些进展的同时，报告也指出成本上升。
senses.why: Two things placed side by side in speech are either simultaneous or being weighed against each other.
senses.whyCN: 在言语中被并排放置的两个事物，要么同时发生，要么正被相互权衡。

intro.en: Alongside is a transparent compound of along and side, and its life began with ships.
intro.cn: alongside 是 along 与 side 的透明复合词，它的生命从船舶开始。

items.en: The first element goes back to andlang, meaning along the full length.
items.cn: 第一个成分上溯至 andlang，意为沿着整个长度。

items.en: Side meant the flank of a body or object, and it still means a surface or position.
items.cn: side 原指身体或物体的侧面，至今仍指表面或位置。

items.en: The compound was used first for a ship lying next to another ship or a wharf.
items.cn: 这个复合词最初用于一艘船紧靠另一艘船或码头。

items.en: Alongside widened from harbour speech to any object placed at the side of another.
items.cn: alongside 从港口用语扩展到任何放在另一物旁边的东西。

items.en: The phrase work alongside extended the side-by-side picture to cooperation.
items.cn: 短语 work alongside 把并肩的画面延伸到合作。

items.en: Placing two facts alongside each other became a way of saying at the same time or compared with.
items.cn: 把两个事实并排放置，成了「同时」或「相比」的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the two halves and a near-form; the near-meaning group gathers words of position and company.
note.cn: 形近组收两个成分与一个近形词；近义组收表示位置与陪伴的词。

entries.definition: Following the length of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿着某物的长度。

entries.definition: A surface or position at the edge of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物边缘的表面或位置。

entries.definition: At the side of, a shorter near-synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指在……旁边，是更短的近义词。

entries.definition: Immediately beside something.
entries.definitionCN: 指紧挨着某物。

entries.definition: In company with, used for cooperation.
entries.definitionCN: 指与……一道，用于合作语境。

entries.definition: Running at the same distance apart without meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 指以相同距离平行延伸而不相交。

entries.definition: Side by side and facing forward, especially of walkers or boats.
entries.definitionCN: 指并排且面朝前方，尤指行人或船只。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two hulls touching and then transfer the same position to work and to comparison.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两只船壳相贴开始，再把同一位置转移到工作与比较上。

normal.en: Alongside is along plus side: moving along the side puts you beside it.
normal.cn: alongside 是 along 加 side：顺着侧面移动，就把你放到旁边。

normal.en: Two boats alongside have one hull facing the other.
normal.cn: 两艘 alongside 的船，各用一个船壳朝向对方。

normal.en: Work alongside means share the same side of the task.
normal.cn: work alongside 意为共处任务的同一侧。

normal.en: Alongside can also mean at the same time, because two facts can stand side by side.
normal.cn: alongside 也可指同时，因为两个事实可以并排站着。

normal.en: Beside is the shorter cousin; both put something at your side.
normal.cn: beside 是更短的近亲；两者都把某物放在你旁边。

abstract.en: Picture two hulls touching in a harbour, each rocking with the other's motion.
abstract.cn: 想象港里两只船壳相贴，各自随着对方的摇动而摇。

abstract.en: Remove the water and the same position becomes two people sharing a task.
abstract.cn: 把水去掉，同一位置就变成两个人共担一项任务。

abstract.en: Remove the task and it becomes two facts standing side by side in a report.
abstract.cn: 再把任务去掉，它就变成报告里并排站着的两个事实。

examples.en: A police car drove alongside the bus for a mile.
examples.cn: 一辆警车与公交车并行驶了一英里。

examples.en: She learned the craft by working alongside her father.
examples.cn: 她跟着父亲并肩干活，学会了这门手艺。

examples.en: Alongside the new jobs, the town gained a larger market.
examples.cn: 在新增就业的同时，镇上也有了更大的市场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额龙赛的」——额，龙赛的船并排靠在一起

root: along（沿着，古英语 andlang）+ side（侧面，古英语 side）构成的复合词；最初用于船舶并排靠泊，后扩展到并肩合作、同时与相比。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses keep two things at one side of each other, whether hulls, workers, events, or figures.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都让两个事物处在彼此的同一侧，无论是船壳、工人、事件还是数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hulls touch in a harbour, and each boat turns one flank toward the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只船壳在港里相贴，每条船都把一侧船舷朝向对方。

branches.en: THE HULL: the first sense is a thing placed at the side of another.
branches.cn: 船壳线：第一个义项是把一物放在另一物的侧面。

branches.en: THE PARALLEL: two objects keep the same distance and the same direction.
branches.cn: 平行线：两个物体保持相同距离与相同方向。

branches.en: THE CREW: people at the same side of a task become partners.
branches.cn: 同伴线：处在任务同一侧的人成为伙伴。

branches.en: THE TIMELINE: two events placed side by side are simultaneous or compared.
branches.cn: 时间线：并排放置的两个事件要么同时，要么被比较。

branches.en: THE SIDE: one word covers physical position and human cooperation.
branches.cn: 侧面线：同一个词既覆盖物理位置，也覆盖人的合作。

intro.en: Alongside is a compound of two native English words, so its parts are transparent and its family is small.
intro.cn: alongside 是两个本土英语词的复合，成分透明，词族不大。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Old English, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都属于古英语，因此拉丁条目为空。

items.example: The tug stayed alongside the ship.
items.exampleCN: 拖船一直靠在大船旁边。

items.example: The left side is painted blue.
The crate stood alongside of the door.
The mayor stood alongside the workers.
The two paintings hang alongside each other.

definition_zh: 出声地；大声地；高声地
definition_en: in a voice that can be heard by others, rather than silently
core_image: 声音离开嘴巴，越过房间，落进另一个人的耳朵
scene: 图书馆里孩子捧着诗集，老师让他读出声来。The teacher asked the boy to read the poem aloud.
sceneCN: 这里 aloud 是「出声地」（第 1 个义项：发出能被听见的声音）；句意为老师让男孩把这首诗朗读出来。

pos.zh: 副词：出声地；大声地；高声地

collocations.zh: 把想法说出声；自言自语

derivatives.zh: 同源形容词，义为「大声的；响亮的」，aloud 的前身即由它加前缀构成
由 loud 加 -ly 构成，义为「大声地；响亮地」，强调音量
由 loud 加 -ness 构成，义为「响亮；音量」
loud 与 speaker 的复合词，义为「扬声器；喇叭」，把声音放大送出

senses.title: In a voice that can be heard
senses.definition: in a voice loud enough to be heard by other people, not in silence
senses.definitionCN: 用足以让别人听见的声音，而非默不作声
senses.example: She read the letter aloud so that everyone in the room could hear it.
senses.exampleCN: 她把信读出声来，让屋里每个人都能听见。
senses.why: The a- here is a worn form of on, the same small prefix in asleep and alive; aloud is a voice switched on and turned outward.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 a- 是 on 的弱化形式，和 asleep、alive 里那个小前缀一样；aloud 就是被打开并朝外送出的声音。

senses.title: Loudly and with force
senses.definition: with a strong, carrying voice, often in a shout or a call
senses.definitionCN: 用响亮、能传远的声音，常指呼喊或叫喊
senses.example: He cried aloud for help when he saw the smoke.
senses.exampleCN: 他看到浓烟时大声呼救。
senses.why: The same word can raise the volume: what is spoken aloud can also be thrown across a room as a shout.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也可以把音量抬高：出声说出的东西，也能作为喊叫抛过整个房间。

senses.title: Thinking aloud
senses.definition: in the phrase think aloud, to speak one's thoughts as they form instead of keeping them silent
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 think aloud，指把正在形成的想法直接说出来，而非闷在心里
senses.example: The engineer thought aloud while tracing the fault in the circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师排查电路故障时把想法说了出来。
senses.why: When thought is spoken as it forms, the mind borrows the outward voice and makes private reasoning audible.
senses.whyCN: 当想法在形成时就被说出，头脑借用了朝外的声音，让私下的推理变得可听见。

intro.en: Aloud is a small English word built on loud, and its history is the history of sound being turned outward.
intro.cn: aloud 是建立在 loud 之上的小型英语词，它的历史就是声音被朝外送出的历史。

items.en: The root *kleu- is reconstructed as 'to hear', and it underlies a wide family of hearing words across Indo-European.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *kleu- 一般重构为「听见」，它支撑着印欧语系中一大族与听觉有关的词。

items.en: Old English hlud meant 'loud, noisy', the quality of a sound that fills the ear.
items.cn: 古英语 hlud 意为「响亮的、喧闹的」，指充满耳朵的那种声音特质。

items.en: The a- of aloud is a reduced form of the preposition on, the same element seen in alive and asleep.
items.cn: aloud 的 a- 是介词 on 的弱化形式，和 alive、asleep 中见到的是同一个成分。

items.en: Aloud is recorded in the fourteenth century with the sense 'in a loud voice, with noise'.
items.cn: aloud 在十四世纪有记录，当时的含义是「用响亮的声音、带着喧闹」。

items.en: The sense softened from 'noisily' to 'in a voice that can be heard', in contrast with silent reading.
items.cn: 词义从「喧闹地」软化为「以能被听见的声音」，与默读形成对照。

items.en: Read aloud and think aloud fixed the word in two everyday phrases about making text or thought audible.
items.cn: read aloud 与 think aloud 把这个词固定在两个日常短语里，一个让文字发声，一个让想法发声。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers loud and its close forms; the near-meaning group gathers ways of saying something audibly.
note.cn: 形近组收 loud 及其近形词；近义组收表示「出声说出」的各种说法。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning strong in sound, easily heard.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「响亮的、容易听见的」。

entries.definition: The adverb from loud, meaning with great volume.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loud 构成的副词，义为「大声地、音量很大地」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to permit, which looks close to aloud but is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「允许」，拼写与 aloud 相近但并无词源关系。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for speaking so that others can hear.
entries.definitionCN: 日常短语，指说出声让别人听见。

entries.definition: In a way that can be heard, with less stress on volume.
entries.definitionCN: 指以能被听见的方式，对音量的强调较弱。

entries.definition: With high volume, closer to the shout sense of aloud.
entries.definitionCN: 指音量大，更接近 aloud 的呼喊义。

entries.definition: By means of the voice, often in contrast with writing.
entries.definitionCN: 指借助嗓音，常与书面表达相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a voice leaving the mouth and then move from reading to shouting to thinking.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从声音离开嘴巴开始，再从朗读移到呼喊，最后移到思考。

normal.en: Aloud is a plus loud: switch a loud voice on and the sound reaches other ears.
normal.cn: aloud 就是 a 加 loud：把一个响亮的声音打开，声音就传到别人耳中。

normal.en: Read aloud means the page leaves your head and enters the room.
normal.cn: read aloud 意为书页离开你的脑袋，进入房间。

normal.en: Think aloud means your inner voice steps outside for a walk.
normal.cn: think aloud 意为内心的声音走到外面散步。

normal.en: If another person can hear it, it was said aloud; if not, it stayed inside.
normal.cn: 如果别人能听见，它就是 aloud 说出的；听不见，它就留在里面。

normal.en: The a- in aloud matches the a- in asleep and alive: a state switched on.
normal.cn: aloud 里的 a- 与 asleep、alive 里的 a- 一致：一种被打开的状态。

abstract.en: Picture a library where one boy's whisper grows just enough to cross the aisle.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，一个男孩的耳语刚好大到能穿过过道。

abstract.en: Now the same voice rises until it fills a stairwell and someone far below answers.
abstract.cn: 然后同一个声音升高，填满楼梯间，下面很远有人回应。

abstract.en: Finally the voice has no listener: it is thought speaking to itself in the open.
abstract.cn: 最后这个声音没有听者：那是想法在开阔处自言自语。

examples.en: She read the letter aloud so that everyone could hear the news.
examples.cn: 她把信读出声来，让大家都能听到这个消息。

examples.en: He cried aloud in pain when the door slammed on his hand.
examples.cn: 门夹到他的手时，他痛得大声叫喊。

examples.en: The designer thought aloud while sketching the new layout.
examples.cn: 设计师画新布局时把想法说了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，唠的」——啊，唠唠叨叨地出声说出来

root: 古英语 hlūd（响亮的，与「听见」同源）+ 前缀 a-（介词 on 的弱化形式，表示处于某种状态），本义「以响亮的方式」，后转指「出声地」。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses move from simply being audible, through sheer volume, to the special case of speaking one's thoughts.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从「能被听见」出发，经过纯粹的「音量大」，最后到「把想法说出声」这一特殊情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice leaves the mouth, crosses the room, and lands in another person's ear.
core.cn: 核心意象：声音离开嘴巴，穿过房间，落进另一个人的耳朵。

branches.en: THE VOICE: the first sense is sound made audible rather than held silent.
branches.cn: 嗓音线：第一个义项是让声音可被听见，而不是保持沉默。

branches.en: THE VOLUME: the same word can lift the voice from speech to a shout.
branches.cn: 音量线：同一个词能把嗓音从说话抬到喊叫。

branches.en: THE CALL: a cry aloud is a message thrown across distance.
branches.cn: 呼喊线：cry aloud 是把消息抛过距离。

branches.en: THE INNER VOICE: thinking aloud lets private speech become public.
branches.cn: 内心线：think aloud 让私下的言语变成公开的。

branches.en: THE EAR: every branch depends on someone or something able to hear.
branches.cn: 耳朵线：每一条分支都依赖某个能听见的人或物。

intro.en: Aloud is one adverb with a small, native family, so the list mixes its base, its relatives and its fixed phrases.
intro.cn: aloud 是一个副词，词族小而本土，因此条目混合了它的基础词、亲属词与固定短语。

latinIntro.en: The word is wholly English in form, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的形式完全属于英语，因此不列拉丁条目。

items.meaning: in a voice that is heard

items.example: She knocked loudly on the door.
The loudness of the alarm woke the street.
items.exampleCN: 警报的音量吵醒了整条街。

items.meaning: a device that sends out sound
items.example: The announcement came through the loudspeaker.
He read aloud to the class.
She thought aloud about the plan.
items.exampleCN: 她把对这个计划的考虑说了出来。

definition_zh: 字母表；字母系统；基础知识；符号系统
definition_en: the ordered set of letters used to write a language, or a similar fixed set of signs
core_image: 阿尔法与贝塔站在最前，其余字母在它们身后排成一行

pos.zh: 名词：字母表；字母系统；基础知识；符号系统

senses.title: The letters of a language
senses.definition: the complete set of letters used to write a particular language
senses.definitionCN: 用来书写某一语言的完整字母集合
senses.example: The English alphabet has twenty-six letters.
senses.exampleCN: 英语字母表有二十六个字母。
senses.why: Alpha and beta are simply the first two Greek letters; naming the whole set after its first pair turned that pair into the name of the series.
senses.whyCN: alpha 与 beta 原本只是头两个希腊字母；用这头一对来命名整套字母，于是这一对就成了整个序列的名字。

senses.title: The fixed order of the letters
senses.definition: the established sequence of the letters, used for listing, indexing, and sorting
senses.definitionCN: 字母既定的排列次序，用于列举、编索引与排序
senses.example: The names on the list are arranged by the alphabet, not by age.
senses.exampleCN: 名单上的名字按字母顺序排列，而不是按年龄。
senses.why: Once the letters are fixed in order, the order itself becomes a tool: dictionaries, indexes and catalogues all run along that row.
senses.whyCN: 字母一旦按次序固定，这个次序本身就成了工具：词典、索引与目录都沿着这一行排列。

senses.title: The basic elements of a subject
senses.definition: the first principles or smallest units that a beginner must learn in a field
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域初学者必须掌握的基本原理或最小单位
senses.example: For a young cook, heat, salt and time are the alphabet of the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 对年轻的厨师来说，火候、盐与时间就是厨房里的基础知识。
senses.why: Learning a subject starts with its smallest units; the alphabet of a field is the set of signs one must know before reading any further.
senses.whyCN: 学习一门学问从最小的单位开始；一个领域的 alphabet 就是继续往下读之前必须先认识的那套符号。

senses.title: A fixed set of signs or code
senses.definition: any closed inventory of signs, such as a phonetic or telegraph alphabet, used to encode messages
senses.definitionCN: 任何封闭的符号清单，如音标字母表或电报码，用来给信息编码
senses.example: Pilots spell out names with the phonetic alphabet to avoid confusion.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员用音标字母表拼读名称，以免混淆。
senses.why: Any code that maps meaning onto a closed set of signs repeats the alphabet pattern: a fixed inventory plus rules for combining it.
senses.whyCN: 任何把意义映射到一套封闭符号上的编码，都在重复字母表的模式：一份固定的清单，加上组合规则。

intro.en: Alphabet is named after its first two letters, and that habit of naming a series by its opening pair is older than the word itself.
intro.cn: alphabet 以它的前两个字母命名，而用开头一对来命名整个序列的习惯比这个词本身更古老。

items.en: The Greek letter names alpha and beta are usually traced to Phoenician aleph 'ox' and beth 'house'.
items.cn: 希腊字母名 alpha 与 beta 通常上溯至腓尼基语的 aleph「牛」与 beth「房屋」。

items.en: Greek joined the first two names into alphabetos, a word for the whole set of letters.
items.cn: 希腊语把开头两个名字合成 alphabetos，用来指整套字母。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as alphabetum, keeping both the letter names and the sense of an ordered series.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 alphabetum，既保留字母名，也保留「有序序列」的含义。

items.en: English alphabet appears in the fifteenth century and soon covered any ordered letter series, not only Greek.
items.cn: 英语 alphabet 于十五世纪出现，很快就不限于希腊字母，而指任何有序的字母序列。

items.en: With printing and dictionaries the fixed order became a practical tool for indexing and sorting.
items.cn: 随着印刷术与词典的发展，固定次序成了编索引与排序的实用工具。

items.en: The phrase the alphabet of a subject extended the letter set to the basic elements of any field.
items.cn: 短语 the alphabet of a subject 把字母集合延伸到任何领域的基本要素。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Greek letter names and the derived adjectives; the near-meaning group gathers other names for writing systems.
note.cn: 形近组收希腊字母名与派生形容词；近义组收书写系统的其他说法。

entries.definition: The first Greek letter, whose name begins the word alphabet.
entries.definitionCN: 第一个希腊字母，它的名字是 alphabet 的开头。

entries.definition: The second Greek letter, whose name ends the word alphabet.
entries.definitionCN: 第二个希腊字母，它的名字是 alphabet 的结尾。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to an alphabet.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「与字母表有关的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for a code that uses both letters and digits.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指同时使用字母与数字的编码。

entries.definition: The general term for any system that records language in visible signs.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何用可见符号记录语言的系统。

entries.definition: A particular set of written characters, such as Latin or Cyrillic.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一套书写字符，如拉丁字母或西里尔字母。

entries.definition: The full inventory of signs available in a writing or coding system.
entries.definitionCN: 某一书写或编码系统中可用的全部符号清单。

entries.definition: An informal word for the alphabet or the first basics of a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 口语说法，指字母表，或某学科的最基础知识。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with the first two Greek letters and then stretch the same row into order, basics and code.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从开头两个希腊字母开始，再把同一行延伸到顺序、基础与编码。

normal.en: Alpha and beta are the first two Greek letters; say them and you have named the whole set.
normal.cn: alpha 与 beta 是头两个希腊字母；念出它们，你就命名了整套字母。

normal.en: The alphabet is a row of letters standing in a fixed order, like runners at a starting line.
normal.cn: alphabet 是一排按固定次序站好的字母，像起跑线上的选手。

normal.en: Once the order is fixed, a dictionary can point to any word by that row.
normal.cn: 次序一旦固定，词典就能沿着这一行找到任何词。

normal.en: The alphabet of a subject is its smallest set of signs, the letters you must know first.
normal.cn: 一个学科的 alphabet 就是它最小的符号集合，是你必须先认识的那些字母。

normal.en: Alphabetical simply means arranged along that row, from the first letter to the last.
normal.cn: alphabetical 意思就是沿着这一行排列，从第一个字母到最后一个。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom wall where the letters march from left to right and never change places.
abstract.cn: 想象教室的墙上，字母从左到右列队，从不换位置。

abstract.en: Move that row into a dictionary and every entry finds its slot by the same march.
abstract.cn: 把这一行搬进词典，每个词条都靠同样的队列找到自己的位置。

abstract.en: Shrink the row to a handful of signs and it becomes any code that spells a message.
abstract.cn: 把这一行缩成少量符号，它就变成任何能拼出信息的编码。

examples.en: Children learn the alphabet before they learn to spell.
examples.cn: 孩子们先学字母表，再学拼写。

examples.en: Please arrange the files by the alphabet, from A to Z.
examples.cn: 请按字母顺序把这些文件从 A 排到 Z。

examples.en: For a beginner, the alphabet of cooking is heat, salt and time.
examples.cn: 对初学者来说，烹饪的基础就是火候、盐和时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿尔法贝特」——阿尔法、贝塔，头两个希腊字母拼成字母表

root: 希腊语 alpha（阿尔法）+ beta（贝塔），即前两个希腊字母之名合称整套字母；经拉丁语 alphabetum 进入英语，后引申为「基础知识」与「符号系统」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the letter set itself, to its fixed order, to the basic signs of a subject, to any coded sign system.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从字母集合本身出发，到它的固定次序，再到某学科的基本符号，最后到任何编码符号系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: alpha and beta stand first, and the rest of the letters line up behind them in a fixed row.
core.cn: 核心意象：alpha 与 beta 站在最前，其余字母在它们身后排成固定的一行。

branches.en: THE LETTER SET: the first sense is the full inventory of letters for a language.
branches.cn: 字母集线：第一个义项是一门语言完整的字母清单。

branches.en: THE ROW: fixed order turns the set into a tool for lists and dictionaries.
branches.cn: 队列线：固定次序把字母集变成列表与词典的工具。

branches.en: THE CODE: a closed set of signs plus rules can spell messages of any length.
branches.cn: 编码线：一套封闭符号加上规则，就能拼出任意长度的信息。

branches.en: THE FIRST LESSON: the alphabet of a subject is what a beginner must learn first.
branches.cn: 入门线：一个学科的 alphabet 是初学者首先要学的东西。

branches.en: THE INVENTORY: every branch rests on a small, finite set of signs.
branches.cn: 清单线：每一条分支都依赖一套小而有限的符号。

intro.en: Alphabet carries two Greek letter names inside it, and its derivatives are built with ordinary English suffixes.
intro.cn: alphabet 内部带着两个希腊字母名，它的派生词由普通英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form alphabetum is the direct source of the English word, but it is not a productive Latin affix here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式 alphabetum 是英语词的直接来源，但在这里并不是能产的拉丁词缀。
